sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十四】起屠維赤奮若七月，盡玄黓執徐九月，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 54] From the seventh month of the jiyou year to the ninth month of the xuanmou year, altogether a little more than three years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, Section 54] From the seventh month of the year jiyou through the ninth month of the year xuanmou—a span of somewhat more than three years.

translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the annals of Emperor Xianzong, styled Zhao Wen Zhang Wu Da Sheng Zhi Shen Xiao, Yuanhe year 4 (

translations.literal: jichou, corresponding to the year 809 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jichou [in the sexagenary cycle], equivalent to 809 CE)

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬戌，御史中丞李夷簡彈京兆尹楊憑，前為江西觀察使，貪污僭侈。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renxu, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian impeached the Metropolitan Governor Yang Ping, who had formerly served as Jiangxi observation commissioner, for corruption and extravagant presumption.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day renxu, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian impeached Metropolitan Governor Yang Ping—formerly Jiangxi observation commissioner—for corruption and arrogant extravagance.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，貶憑臨賀尉。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Yang Ping was demoted to commandant of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Yang Ping was demoted to the post of commandant of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 夷簡，元懿之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Yijian was a great-great-grandson of Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian was a great-great-grandson of Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 上命盡籍憑資產，李絳諫曰：「舊制，非反逆不籍其家。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that all of Ping's property be registered and confiscated. Li Jiang remonstrated, saying, "By old regulation, one does not register and confiscate a household unless the crime is treason."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yang Ping's entire estate registered and seized. Li Jiang objected: "Under longstanding rule, a household is not inventoried and confiscated unless the offense is treason."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then relented.

sentences.zh: 憑之親友無敢送者，櫟陽尉徐晦獨至藍田與別。

translations.literal: None of Ping's kin and friends dared to see him off; only the Liyang commandant Xu Hui went alone to Lantian to bid him farewell.
translations.idiomatic: None of Yang Ping's friends or relatives dared see him off; only Xu Hui, commandant of Liyang, went alone to Lantian to take his leave.

sentences.zh: 太常卿權德輿素與晦善，謂之曰：「君送楊臨賀，誠為厚矣，無乃為累乎！」

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies Quan Deyu, who had long been on good terms with Hui, said to him, "You have indeed shown great kindness in seeing off Yang of Linhe, but might this not bring trouble upon you!"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Quan Deyu, who had long been friendly with Xu Hui, told him, "Your farewell to Yang of Linhe is truly generous—but are you not inviting trouble for yourself?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「晦自布衣蒙楊公知獎，今日遠謫，豈得不與之別！

translations.literal: He replied, "Since I was a commoner I have received Yang's recognition and encouragement; now that he is banished far away, how could I fail to take leave of him!
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "From the days when I was a commoner, Master Yang recognized and encouraged me. Now that he is exiled so far away, how could I not bid him farewell?

sentences.zh: 借如明公它日為讒人所逐，晦敢自同路人乎！」

translations.literal: If someday Your Excellency were driven out by slanderers, would Hui dare to treat you like a mere passerby!"
translations.idiomatic: If someday you were cast out by slanderers, would I dare treat you as a stranger on the road?"

sentences.zh: 德輿嗟歎，稱之於朝。

translations.literal: Deyu sighed in admiration and praised him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu sighed in admiration and commended him at court.

sentences.zh: 後數日，李夷簡奏為監察御史。

translations.literal: Several days later, Li Yijian memorialized that he be appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, Li Yijian recommended him for appointment as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 晦謝曰：「晦平生未嘗得望公顏色，公何從而取之！」

translations.literal: Hui thanked him and said, "In all my life Hui has never once beheld Your Excellency's countenance—how did you come to select me!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hui thanked him and said, "I have never even seen your face in my life—how did you choose me?"

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「君不負楊臨賀，肯負國乎！」

translations.literal: Yijian said, "You did not fail Yang of Linhe—would you fail the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Yijian said, "You did not betray Yang of Linhe—would you betray the state?"

sentences.zh: 上密問諸學士曰：「今欲用王承宗為成德留後，割其德、棣二州更為一鎮以離其勢，並使承宗輸二稅，請官吏，一如師道，何如？』

translations.literal: The emperor secretly questioned the academicians, saying, "We now wish to appoint Wang Chengzong military commissioner of Chengde, to carve off his two prefectures De and Di and make them a separate command to divide his power, and also to have Chengzong submit the two taxes and request court officials, just as with Shidao—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor privately asked the Hanlin academicians: "We intend to confirm Wang Chengzong as acting commissioner of Chengde, detach his prefectures of De and Di into a separate command to weaken him, and require Chengzong to remit the two taxes and accept court-appointed officials, as with Li Shidao—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 李絳等對曰：「德、棣之隸成德，為日已久，今一旦割之，恐承宗及其將士憂疑怨望，得以為辭。

translations.literal: Li Jiang and others replied, "De and Di have been subordinate to Chengde for a long time; to sever them at a stroke now will likely make Chengzong and his officers and soldiers anxious, suspicious, resentful, and discontented, giving them a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang and the others answered: "De and Di have belonged to Chengde for many years. To cut them away all at once may fill Chengzong and his troops with anxiety, suspicion, and resentment—and give them a ready excuse.

sentences.zh: 況其鄰道情狀一同，各慮它日分割，或潛相構扇。

translations.literal: Moreover, the neighboring circuits are in the same situation; each fears future partition, and they may secretly incite one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, neighboring circuits are in the same position; each will fear being carved up later and may secretly stir one another up.

sentences.zh: 萬一旅拒，倍難處置，願更三思。

translations.literal: If by any chance they resist in a body, disposition will be twice as difficult; we beg Your Majesty to reconsider thrice.
translations.idiomatic: If they should resist en masse, the situation would be twice as hard to manage. We urge Your Majesty to think again.

sentences.zh: 所是二稅、官吏，願因弔祭使至彼，自以其意諭承宗，令上表陳乞如師道例，勿令知出陛下意。

translations.literal: As for the two taxes and officials, we wish that when the condolence envoy reaches there, he explain in his own words to Chengzong and have him memorialize and petition as in Shidao's case, without letting him know it came from Your Majesty's mind.
translations.idiomatic: On the two taxes and court officials, we suggest sending the condolence envoy to explain in his own words and have Chengzong petition on the Li Shidao model—without letting him know the idea originated with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 如此，則幸而聽命，於理固順，若其不聽，體亦無損。」

translations.literal: In this way, if by good fortune he obeys, it is in principle proper; if he does not obey, the court's standing is still unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: If he complies, all the better and the arrangement is orderly; if he refuses, the court loses nothing in principle."

sentences.zh: 上又問：「今劉濟、田季安皆有疾，若其物故，豈可盡如成德付授其子，天下何時當平！

translations.literal: The emperor asked again, "Liu Ji and Tian Ji'an are both ill; if they die, can we simply hand over their posts to their sons as with Chengde—when will the realm ever be pacified!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again: "Liu Ji and Tian Ji'an are both ill. If they die, can we keep handing their commands to their sons as with Chengde? When will the empire ever be at peace?

sentences.zh: 議者皆言『宜乘此際代之，不受則發兵討之，時不要失。』

translations.literal: Those in council all say, 'We ought to seize this moment to replace them; if they do not accept, then send troops to punish them—the opportune moment must not be lost.'
translations.idiomatic: Counselors all say we should seize this moment to replace them, and if they refuse, send armies to punish them—the opportunity must not be missed.'

sentences.zh: 如何？」

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What is your view?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「群臣見陛下西取蜀，東取吳，易於反掌，故諂諛躁競之人爭獻策畫，勸開河北，不為國家深謀遠慮，陛下亦以前日成功之易而信其言。

translations.literal: They replied, "The ministers see that Your Majesty took Shu in the west and Wu in the east as easily as turning the hand, so flatterers and the rash and ambitious vie to offer plans, urging war in Hebei, without deep and far-sighted counsel for the state; Your Majesty also, because of yesterday's easy success, believes their words.
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "Your ministers see how easily you took Shu in the west and Wu in the east, so sycophants and the ambitious rush forward with plans urging campaigns in Hebei—without deep, far-sighted counsel for the realm. Your Majesty, too, trusts them because recent victories came so easily.

sentences.zh: 臣等夙夜思之，河北之勢與二方異。

translations.literal: We have pondered this day and night: the situation in Hebei differs from those two regions.
translations.idiomatic: We have thought on this day and night: Hebei's position is not like that of the other two regions.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 西川、浙西皆非反側之地，其四鄰皆國家臂指之臣。

translations.literal: Xichuan and Zhexi were neither lands of rebellion; on all four sides their neighbors were ministers at the court's beck and call.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan and Zhexi were not rebel heartlands; on every side their neighbors were officials who moved at the court's command.

sentences.zh: 劉辟、李錡獨生狂謀，其下皆莫之與，辟、錡徒以貨財啖之，大軍一臨，則渙然離耳。

translations.literal: Liu Pi and Li Qi alone conceived mad schemes; none below followed them—Pi and Qi could only buy men with goods and wealth; once the great army arrived, they scattered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi and Li Qi alone nursed reckless plots; their subordinates would not follow them. Pi and Qi could only buy loyalty with wealth; when the imperial army arrived, their forces melted away.

sentences.zh: 故臣等當時亦勸陛下誅之，以其萬全故也。

translations.literal: Therefore we too then urged Your Majesty to execute them, because the plan was wholly secure.
translations.idiomatic: That is why we too urged Your Majesty to strike them then—the odds were entirely in our favor.

sentences.zh: 成德則不然，內則膠固歲深，外則蔓連勢廣，其將士百姓懷其累代煦嫗之恩，不知君臣逆順之理，諭之不從，威之不服，將為朝廷羞。

translations.literal: Chengde is not so: inwardly it has been glued fast for many years; outwardly its tendrils spread and its power is wide. Its officers, soldiers, and common people cherish the warmth and nurture of generations and do not know the principle of lord and subject, obedience and rebellion; admonish them and they will not heed, threaten them and they will not submit—it will bring shame on the court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde is different: inwardly it has been bound tight for years; outwardly its influence spreads far and wide. Its troops and people remember generations of kindly rule and do not grasp the logic of loyalty and rebellion. Persuasion will not move them, threats will not cow them—and the court will be shamed.

sentences.zh: 又，鄰道平居或相猜恨，及聞代易，必合為一心，蓋各為子孫之謀，亦慮他日及此故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, neighboring circuits in ordinary times may suspect and hate one another, but on hearing of replacement and transfer they will surely unite as one heart—for each plots for his descendants and also fears that someday this will befall him.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring circuits may distrust one another in normal times, but once they hear of forced succession they will unite—for each is scheming for his heirs and fears the same fate tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 萬一餘道或相表裡，兵連禍結，財盡力竭，西戎、北狄乘間窺窬，其為憂患可勝道哉！

translations.literal: If by any chance the other circuits act in concert inside and out, war links with calamity, wealth is exhausted and strength spent, and the western barbarians and northern Di seize the gap to peer and pry—can the resulting troubles even be told!
translations.idiomatic: If other circuits join forces, war and disaster chain together, treasury and strength are drained, and western and northern peoples seize the opening to strike—how many woes would follow!

sentences.zh: 濟、季安與承宗事體不殊，若物故之際，有間可乘，當臨事圖之。

translations.literal: Ji, Ji'an, and Chengzong are not different in kind; if at the time of death an opening can be seized, we should plan when the moment comes.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, Ji'an, and Chengzong are in the same case; when death opens a chance, we should plan at the time.

sentences.zh: 於今用兵，則恐未可。

translations.literal: To use arms now is perhaps not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: To resort to arms now is probably premature.

sentences.zh: 太平之業，非朝夕可致，願陛下審處之。」

translations.literal: The enterprise of great peace cannot be achieved in a morning or an evening; we beg Your Majesty to weigh it carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Great peace cannot be won overnight; we ask Your Majesty to judge the matter with care."

sentences.zh: 時吳少誠病甚，降等復上言：「少誠病必不起。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shaocheng was gravely ill; Jiang and the others again submitted, "Shaocheng's illness will surely not allow recovery.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Shaocheng was gravely ill. Li Jiang and the others submitted again: "Shaocheng will not recover from this illness.

sentences.zh: 淮西事體與河北不同，四旁皆國家州縣，不與賊鄰，無黨援相助。

translations.literal: The situation in Huaixi differs from Hebei: on all four sides are the state's prefectures and counties; it does not border on bandits and has no partisan allies to aid it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixi's situation differs from Hebei's: it is surrounded on every side by imperial prefectures and counties, borders no rebel territory, and has no allies to support it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命帥，今正其時，萬一不從，可議征討。

translations.literal: For the court to appoint a commander is exactly timely now; if by any chance they do not obey, we may discuss punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the moment for the court to appoint a commissioner; if they refuse, we can discuss a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 臣願捨恆冀難致之策，就申蔡易成之謀。

translations.literal: Your servants wish to abandon the hard-to-attain plan for Heng and Ji and adopt the easy-to-succeed plan for Shen and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: We urge abandoning the hard strategy against Heng and Ji in favor of the easier plan against Shen and Cai.

sentences.zh: 脫或恆冀連兵，事未如意，蔡州有釁，勢可興師，南北之役俱興，財力之用不足。

translations.literal: If perchance Heng and Ji link arms in war and matters do not go as wished, while Cai Prefecture offers a breach and troops may be raised, campaigns north and south will both flare and fiscal and military resources will not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If Heng and Ji fight together and things go badly while Caizhou offers an opening for war, campaigns on both fronts would drain treasury and strength beyond our means.

sentences.zh: 儻事不得已，須赦承宗，則恩德虛施，威令頓廢。

translations.literal: If matters reach the point where we must pardon Chengzong, then grace will have been spent in vain and authority and command abruptly voided.
translations.idiomatic: If we are forced to pardon Chengzong, imperial favor will have been wasted and authority collapsed at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 不如早賜處分，以收鎮冀之心，坐待機宜，必獲申蔡之利。」

translations.literal: It would be better to grant disposition early, to win the hearts of Zhen and Ji, sit and await the opportune moment, and surely gain the advantage over Shen and Cai."
translations.idiomatic: Better to settle Chengzong early, win over Zhen and Ji, wait for the right moment, and secure the advantage in Shen and Cai."

sentences.zh: 既而承宗久未得朝命，頗懼，累表自訴。

translations.literal: Before long Chengzong, having long received no court order, was quite afraid and repeatedly memorialized in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, having waited long without word from court, Chengzong grew fearful and memorialized repeatedly in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午，上乃遣京兆少尹裴武詣真定宣慰，承宗受詔甚恭，曰：「三軍見迫，不暇俟朝旨，請獻德、棣二州以明懇款。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day renwu, the emperor then sent the Metropolitan Vice Prefect Pei Wu to Zhending to proclaim consolation. Chengzong received the edict very respectfully and said, "The three armies pressed me; I had no leisure to await the court's command. I beg to offer the two prefectures De and Di to show my earnest sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renwu, the emperor sent Metropolitan Vice Prefect Pei Wu to Zhending on a mission of consolation. Chengzong received the edict with great deference and said: "My armies pressed me; I could not wait for court instructions. I offer De and Di to prove my sincerity."

sentences.zh: 丙申，安南都護張舟奏破環王三萬眾。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Protector-General of Annan Zhang Zhou memorialized that he had defeated thirty thousand men of Huan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhang Zhou, protector-general of Annan, reported defeating thirty thousand troops of Huan.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲辰朔，裴武覆命。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day jiachen, Pei Wu returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day jiachen, Pei Wu returned to report his mission.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以承宗為成德軍節度、恆、冀、深、趙州觀察使，德州刺史薛昌朝為保信軍節度、德、棣二州觀察使。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Chengzong was made military commissioner of the Chengde army and observation commissioner of Heng, Ji, Shen, and Zhao prefectures; the Dezhou prefect Xue Changchao was made military commissioner of the Baoxin army and observation commissioner of De and Di prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Wang Chengzong was appointed military commissioner of Chengde and observation commissioner of Heng, Ji, Shen, and Zhao; Xue Changchao, prefect of Dezhou, was made military commissioner of Baoxin and observation commissioner of De and Di.

sentences.zh: 昌朝，嵩之子，王氏之婿也，故就用之。

translations.literal: Changchao was a son of Xue Song and a son-in-law of the Wang clan; therefore he was employed.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao was Xue Song's son and a Wang son-in-law; that is why he was chosen.

sentences.zh: 田季安得飛報，先知之，使謂承宗曰：「昌朝陰與朝廷通，故受節鉞。」

translations.literal: Tian Ji'an received an urgent report and knew first; he sent word to Chengzong, saying, "Changchao secretly communicates with the court—that is why he received the commissioner's seal and baton."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an learned first by urgent dispatch and sent word to Chengzong: "Changchao is in secret contact with court—that is why he received the commission."

sentences.zh: 承宗遽遣數百騎馳入德州，執昌朝，至真定，囚之。

translations.literal: Chengzong at once sent several hundred horsemen galloping into Dezhou, seized Changchao, brought him to Zhending, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong immediately sent hundreds of horsemen into Dezhou, seized Changchao, brought him to Zhending, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 中使送昌朝節過魏州，季安陽為宴勞，留使者累日，比至德州，已不及矣。

translations.literal: The palace envoy bearing Changchao's commission passed through Weizhou; Ji'an pretended to host a feast in his honor and detained the envoy for many days; by the time he reached Dezhou, it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy bearing Changchao's commission passed through Weizhou; Ji'an feigned hospitality and detained the envoy for days—by the time he reached Dezhou, it was too late.

sentences.zh: 上以裴武為欺罔，又有譖之者曰：「武使還，先宿裴垍家，明旦乃入見。」

translations.literal: The emperor considered Pei Wu deceitful, and there were also slanderers who said, "When Wu returned from his mission, he first lodged at Pei Ji's house and only the next morning entered audience."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Pei Wu had deceived him. Slanderers also said: "When Wu returned, he stayed first at Pei Ji's house and only saw the emperor the next morning."

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，以語李絳，欲貶武於嶺南。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry, told Li Jiang, and wished to banish Wu to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, told Li Jiang, and wanted to exile Wu to the far south.

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「武昔陷李懷光軍中，守節不屈，豈容今日遽為奸回！

translations.literal: Jiang said, "Wu was once trapped in Li Huai'guang's army and held to his integrity without yielding—how could he today suddenly become a traitor!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said: "Wu was once trapped in Li Huai'guang's camp and held firm without yielding—how could he suddenly be a traitor now?

sentences.zh: 蓋賊多變詐，人未易盡其情。

translations.literal: Bandits are full of shifting deceit; it is not easy to fathom them fully.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels are endlessly deceitful; their true intentions are hard to read.

sentences.zh: 承宗始懼朝廷誅討，故請獻二州。

translations.literal: Chengzong at first feared the court's punitive strike, and therefore asked to offer the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong first feared imperial punishment, which is why he offered the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 既蒙恩貸，而鄰道皆不欲成德開分割之端，計必有陰行間說誘而脅之，使不得守其初心者，非武之罪也。

translations.literal: Having received imperial grace, yet neighboring circuits all did not wish Chengde to open the precedent of partition—there must surely have been covert agents who slandered, enticed, and coerced him so that he could not keep his original intent; this is not Wu's fault.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving imperial favor, neighboring circuits did not want Chengde to set a precedent of partition—surely covert agents slandered and pressured him until he abandoned his first intent. That is not Wu's fault.

sentences.zh: 今陛下選武使入逆亂之地，使還，一語不相應，遽竄之暇荒，臣恐自今奉使賊廷者以武為戒，苟求便身，率為依阿兩可之言，莫肯盡誠具陳利害，如此，非國家之利也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty chose Wu to go as envoy into a land of rebellion and disorder; when he returned, because one word did not match, you would at once banish him to the remote wilds. I fear that from now on envoys to rebel courts will take Wu as a warning, seek only their own safety, and all offer equivocal, accommodating words, unwilling to speak sincerely and set forth advantage and harm—in this way it is not to the state's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sent Wu into rebel territory; because one report did not match expectations, you would exile him to the wilderness. Envoys to rebel courts will take warning from Wu, protect themselves, and offer only safe, equivocal words rather than honest counsel on advantage and harm. That cannot serve the state.

sentences.zh: 且垍、武久處朝廷，諳練事體，豈有使還未見天子而先宿宰相家乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, Ji and Wu have long been at court and are versed in affairs—how could an envoy return and lodge at a chief minister's house before seeing the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Wu have served at court for years and know protocol—how could an envoy lodge at a chief minister's house before seeing the emperor?

sentences.zh: 臣敢為陛下必保其不然，此殆有讒人欲傷武及垍者，願陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Your servant dares assure Your Majesty that it certainly was not so; this is likely slanderers wishing to harm Wu and Ji—may Your Majesty examine it."
translations.idiomatic: I dare assure Your Majesty it did not happen—likely slanderers wished to harm Wu and Ji. I ask Your Majesty to look into it."

sentences.zh: 上良久曰：「理或有此。」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor said, "There may be reason in this."
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor said, "That may well be so."

sentences.zh: 遂不問。

translations.literal: He then pursued the matter no further.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，振武奏吐蕃五萬餘騎至拂梯泉。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Zhenwu reported that more than fifty thousand Tibetan horsemen had reached Futiquan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Zhenwu reported that over fifty thousand Tibetan horsemen had reached Futiquan.

sentences.zh: 辛未，豐州奏吐蕃萬餘騎至大石谷，掠回鶻入貢還國者。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Fengzhou reported that more than ten thousand Tibetan horsemen had reached Dashigu and plundered Uyghurs returning home after presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Fengzhou reported that over ten thousand Tibetan horsemen reached Dashigu and raided Uyghur tribute missions returning home.

sentences.zh: 左神策軍吏李昱貸長安富人錢八千緡，滿三歲不償，京兆尹許孟容收捕械系，立期使償，曰：「期滿不足，當死。」

translations.literal: A clerk of the Left Divine Strategy Army, Li Yu, borrowed eight thousand strings of cash from a rich man of Chang'an; when three years were full he had not repaid. The Metropolitan Governor Xu Mengrong arrested him, put him in fetters, and set a deadline for repayment, saying, "If when the deadline is full the sum is not complete, he shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, a clerk of the Left Divine Strategy Army, borrowed eight thousand strings of cash from a wealthy Chang'an man and failed to repay after three years. Metropolitan Governor Xu Mengrong arrested him in chains and set a deadline: "If the debt is not paid by then, he dies."

sentences.zh: 一軍大驚。

translations.literal: The whole army was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 中尉訴於上，上遣中使宣旨，送本軍，孟容不之遣。

translations.literal: The army superintendent appealed to the emperor; the emperor sent a palace envoy to proclaim the imperial will and have him returned to his army; Mengrong would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: The army superintendent appealed to the emperor, who sent a palace envoy to order Li Yu returned to his unit. Mengrong refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 中使再至，孟容曰：「臣不奉詔，當死。

translations.literal: The palace envoy came again; Mengrong said, "If your servant does not obey the edict, he should die.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came again, Mengrong said: "If I disobey the edict, I deserve death.

sentences.zh: 然臣為陛下尹京畿，非抑制豪強，何以肅清輦下！

translations.literal: Yet your servant serves Your Majesty as governor of the capital region—if he does not restrain the powerful and overbearing, how can he bring order beneath the imperial chariot!
translations.idiomatic: But I govern the capital for Your Majesty—if I do not restrain the powerful, how can I keep order at court?

sentences.zh: 錢未畢償，昱不可得。」

translations.literal: Until the money is fully repaid, Yu cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Until the debt is paid in full, Li Yu will not be released."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其剛直而許之，京城震慄。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his firm uprightness and granted it; the capital trembled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his firmness and approved; the capital was shaken.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使諭王承宗，使遣薛昌朝還鎮。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct Wang Chengzong to send Xue Changchao back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy ordering Wang Chengzong to release Xue Changchao and restore him to his post.

sentences.zh: 承宗不奉詔。

translations.literal: Chengzong did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸未，制削奪承宗官爵，以左神策中尉吐突承璀為左、右神策、河中、河陽、浙西、宣歙等道行營兵馬使、招討處置等使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day guimao, an edict stripped Chengzong of rank and titles and made the Left Divine Strategy Army superintendent Tutu Chengcui camp military commissioner of the Left and Right Divine Strategy, Hezhong, Heyang, Zhexi, Xuan-She, and other circuits, and commissioner for pacification and disposition.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guimao, an edict stripped Chengzong of rank and titles and appointed Tutu Chengcui, superintendent of the Left Divine Strategy Army, as camp military commissioner and pacification commissioner over the Left and Right Divine Strategy armies and the Hezhong, Heyang, Zhexi, and Xuan-She circuits, among others.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士白居易上奏，以為：「國家征伐，當責成將帥，近歲始以中使為監軍。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Bai Juyi submitted a memorial, holding that: "When the state undertakes punitive campaigns, it should charge the generals with responsibility; only in recent years have palace envoys begun to serve as army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Bai Juyi memorialized: "When the state wages war, generals should bear responsibility—only in recent years have palace envoys been made army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有征天下之兵，專令中使統領者也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present there has never been a case of mobilizing the armies of the realm and putting palace envoys alone in overall command.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, no one has mobilized armies across the realm and placed palace envoys in sole command.

sentences.zh: 今神策軍既不置行營節度使，即承璀乃制將也。

translations.literal: Now that the Divine Strategy Army has no camp military commissioner appointed, Chengcui is in effect the commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: Since no camp military commissioner is appointed for the Divine Strategy Army, Chengcui is effectively the commanding general.

sentences.zh: 又充諸軍招討處置使，即承璀乃都統也。

translations.literal: He also serves as pacification and disposition commissioner for all armies—thus Chengcui is in effect supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: He also serves as pacification commissioner for all armies—making him supreme commander in effect.

sentences.zh: 臣恐四方聞之，必輕朝廷；

translations.literal: Your servant fears that when the four quarters hear of this they will surely hold the court in light esteem;
translations.idiomatic: I fear the four quarters will hold the court in contempt when they hear of this;

sentences.zh: 四夷聞之，必笑中國。

translations.literal: when the four barbarians hear of it they will surely laugh at China.
translations.idiomatic: and foreign peoples will laugh at China.

sentences.zh: 陛下忍令後代相傳雲以中官為制將、都統自陛下始乎！

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty bear that posterity will transmit the saying that making eunuchs commanding generals and supreme commanders began with Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Can Your Majesty bear posterity saying that appointing eunuchs as commanding generals and supreme commanders began with you?

sentences.zh: 臣又恐劉濟、茂昭及希朝、從史乃至諸道將校皆恥受承璀指麾，心既不齊，功何由立！

translations.literal: Your servant also fears that Liu Ji, Maozhao, Xichao, Congshi, and the officers of the various circuits will all be ashamed to take orders from Chengcui; if hearts are not united, how can achievement be established!
translations.idiomatic: I also fear Liu Ji, Maozhao, Xichao, Congshi, and officers of every circuit will be ashamed to take orders from Chengcui—if hearts are divided, how can victory be won?

sentences.zh: 此是資承宗之計而挫諸將之勢也。

translations.literal: This is a plan that aids Chengzong and crushes the generals' momentum.
translations.idiomatic: This aids Chengzong and undermines our generals.

sentences.zh: 陛下念承璀勤勞，貴之可也；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty recalls Chengcui's diligent service, you may honor him;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty values Chengcui's loyal service, you may honor him;

sentences.zh: 憐其忠赤，富之可也。

translations.literal: if you pity his loyal devotion, you may enrich him.
translations.idiomatic: if you pity his loyalty, you may enrich him.

sentences.zh: 至於軍國權柄，動關理亂，朝廷制度，出自祖宗，陛下寧忍徇下之情而自隳法制，從人之欲而自損聖明，何不思於一時之間而取笑於萬代之後乎！」

translations.literal: As for military and state authority, which touches order and disorder, court institutions come from the ancestors—can Your Majesty bear to indulge subordinates' feelings and yourself destroy law and regulation, follow men's desires and yourself diminish sagely clarity—why not think for a moment and avoid becoming a laughingstock for ten thousand generations!"
translations.idiomatic: But military and state power bears on order and chaos; court institutions come from the ancestors. Can Your Majesty indulge subordinates, destroy your own laws, follow private wishes, and dim your own glory—without thinking how posterity will laugh?"

sentences.zh: 時諫官、御史論承璀職名太重者相屬，上皆不聽。

translations.literal: At that time remonstrating officials and censors who argued that Chengcui's titles were too weighty followed one after another; the emperor would not heed any.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and censors argued in succession that Chengcui's titles were too grand; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 戊子，上御延英殿，度支使李元素、鹽鐵使李鄘、京兆尹許孟容、御史中丞李夷簡、諫議大夫孟簡、給事中呂元膺、穆質、右補闕獨孤郁等極言其不可。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi the emperor held court in the Yanying Hall; Revenue Commissioner Li Yuansu, Salt and Iron Commissioner Li Yong, Metropolitan Governor Xu Mengrong, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian, Remonstrance Grandee Meng Jian, Attendant-in-Ordinary Lü Yuanying, Mu Zhi, and Right Supplementation Censor Dugu Yu and others spoke to the utmost that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor held court in the Yanying Hall. Revenue Commissioner Li Yuansu, Salt and Iron Commissioner Li Yong, Metropolitan Governor Xu Mengrong, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian, Remonstrance Grandee Meng Jian, Attendants-in-Ordinary Lü Yuanying and Mu Zhi, and Right Supplementation Censor Dugu Yu spoke forcefully against the appointment.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，明日，削承璀四道兵馬使，改處置為宣慰而已。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; the next day he stripped Chengcui of military commissioner over four circuits and changed disposition commissioner to consolation commissioner only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor yielded; the next day he removed Chengcui's authority over four circuits' armies and reduced his title from disposition commissioner to consolation commissioner only.

sentences.zh: 李絳嘗極言宦官驕橫，侵害政事，讒毀忠貞。

translations.literal: Li Jiang had once spoken to the utmost on how eunuchs were arrogant and overbearing, encroached on government affairs, and slandered the loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang had once spoken forcefully of how eunuchs were arrogant, interfered in government, and slandered loyal officials.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此屬安敢為讒！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How would this lot dare to slander!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How would they dare to slander anyone!

sentences.zh: 就使為之，朕亦不聽。」

translations.literal: Even if they did, I would not listen."
translations.idiomatic: Even if they did, I would not listen."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「此屬大抵不知仁義，不分枉直，唯利是嗜，得賂則譽跖、足喬為廉良，怫意則毀龔、黃為貪暴，能用傾巧之智，構成疑似之端，朝夕左右浸潤以入之，陛下必有時而信之矣。

translations.literal: Jiang said, "This lot for the most part do not know benevolence and righteousness, do not distinguish wrong from right, and crave profit alone; given a bribe they praise Zhi and Qiao as honest and good, crossed in will they denounce Gong and Huang as greedy and violent. They can use crafty, overturning intelligence to fabricate grounds of suspicion; day and night, soaking and seeping in at Your Majesty's side, Your Majesty will surely sometimes believe them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said: "They scarcely know benevolence or righteousness, cannot tell right from wrong, and crave profit alone. Bribed, they praise villains as honest; crossed, they denounce the upright as corrupt. With cunning they manufacture suspicion and drip poison into Your Majesty's ear day and night—you will believe them sooner or later.

sentences.zh: 自古宦官敗國者，備載方冊，陛下豈得不防其漸乎！」

translations.literal: From antiquity eunuchs who ruined states are fully recorded in the annals—can Your Majesty fail to guard against the beginning!"
translations.idiomatic: History is full of eunuchs who ruined states—can Your Majesty fail to guard against the first signs?"

sentences.zh: 己亥，吐突承璀將神策兵發長安，命恆州四面籓鎮各進兵招討。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Tutu Chengcui led the Divine Strategy troops out from Chang'an and ordered the feudal commands on all four sides of Hengzhou each to advance troops for pacification.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Tutu Chengcui led the Divine Strategy Army out of Chang'an and ordered the surrounding commands to advance troops for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 初，吳少誠寵其大將吳少陽，名以從弟，署為軍職，出入少誠家如至親，累遷申州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu Shaocheng favored his senior general Wu Shaoyang, calling him a junior cousin, appointed him to military office, and coming and going from Shaocheng's household as if among closest kin; he was promoted in succession to prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Wu Shaocheng had doted on his senior general Wu Shaoyang, calling him a younger cousin. He gave him military posts and treated him like family in his own house, eventually promoting him to prefect of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少誠病，不知人，家僮鮮于熊兒詐以少誠命召少陽攝副使、知軍州事。

translations.literal: When Shaocheng fell ill and lost the ability to recognize people, the household servant Xianyu Xiong'er falsely used Shaocheng's name to summon Shaoyang to serve as deputy commissioner and handle military and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaocheng fell ill and could no longer recognize anyone, a household servant named Xianyu Xiong'er forged orders in Shaocheng's name, summoning Shaoyang to serve as deputy commissioner and take charge of the army and the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少誠有子元慶，少陽殺之。

translations.literal: Shaocheng had a son, Yuanqing; Shaoyang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng had a son named Yuanqing; Shaoyang had him killed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己巳，少誠薨，少陽自為留後。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jisi, Shaocheng died; Shaoyang made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jisi, Shaocheng died, and Shaoyang declared himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，雲南王尋閣勸卒，子勸龍晟立。

translations.literal: That year, the King of Yunnan, Xun Gequan, died; his son Quan Longsheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Xun Gequan, king of Nanzhao, died, and his son Quan Longsheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 田季安聞吐突承璀將兵討王承宗，聚其徒曰：「師不跨河二十五年矣，今一旦越魏伐趙，趙虜，魏亦虜矣，計為之奈何？」

translations.literal: When Tian Ji'an heard that Tutu Chengcui was leading troops to attack Wang Chengzong, he gathered his followers and said, "Imperial armies have not crossed the river for twenty-five years; now in a single stroke they cross Wei to attack Zhao—if Zhao is taken captive, Wei will be taken captive too. What shall we plan to do about this?"
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Ji'an learned that Tutu Chengcui was marching against Wang Chengzong, he assembled his officers and said, "For twenty-five years imperial armies have not crossed the Yellow River. Now they mean to pass through Wei to strike Zhao—and if Zhao falls, Wei will fall next. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 其將有超伍而言者，曰：「願借騎五千，以除君憂！」

translations.literal: Among his generals, one who stepped forward beyond the ranks spoke and said, "I beg to borrow five thousand horsemen to remove your worry!"
translations.idiomatic: One general stepped forward from the ranks and cried, "Give me five thousand cavalry, and I will lift this burden from you!"

sentences.zh: 季安大呼曰：「壯哉！

translations.literal: Ji'an shouted in a great voice, "Magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an cried out, "Splendid!

sentences.zh: 兵決出，格沮者斬！」

translations.literal: The army shall surely march out; whoever obstructs shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: The army will march! Anyone who stands in the way will be executed!
[End of speech.]"

sentences.zh: 幽州牙將絳人譚忠為劉濟使魏，知其謀，入謂季安曰：「如某之謀，是引天下之兵也。

translations.literal: Tan Zhong of Jiang, a gate guard officer of Youzhou, went as Liu Ji's envoy to Wei; learning their plan, he entered and said to Ji'an, "Were one to follow my plan, it would be to summon the armies of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong, a gate officer from Jiang in Youzhou, was sent by Liu Ji as envoy to Wei. When he learned of Tian Ji'an's plan, he went in and said, "If you follow that course, you will bring the armies of the whole empire down upon you.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 今王師越魏伐趙，不使耆臣宿將而專付中臣，不輸天下之甲而多出秦甲，君知誰為之謀？

translations.literal: Now the imperial army crosses Wei to attack Zhao, yet does not employ veteran officials and seasoned generals but entrusts the matter solely to a middle-ranking official; does not supply armor from across the empire but sends out mostly Qin armor—do you know whose plan this is?
translations.idiomatic: The court army is crossing Wei to strike Zhao, yet the emperor has not put veteran ministers and old generals in command—only a middle-ranking eunuch. He is not mobilizing armor from all the provinces but chiefly the Qin armies. Do you know whose design this is?

sentences.zh: 此乃天子自為之謀，欲將誇服於臣下也。

translations.literal: This is the Son of Heaven's own plan, intending to display and triumph before his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: This is the emperor's own scheme—he means to win glory and awe his officials.

sentences.zh: 若師未叩趙而先碎於魏，是上之謀反不如下，且能不恥於天下乎！

translations.literal: If the army has not yet struck Zhao but is first shattered in Wei, then the plan of the superior is worse than that of the inferior—can he fail to be shamed before the empire!
translations.idiomatic: If the army is crushed in Wei before it even reaches Zhao, the emperor's plan will have failed worse than yours—and can he avoid humiliation before the whole realm?

sentences.zh: 既恥且怒，必任智士畫長策，仗猛將練精兵，畢力再舉涉河，鑒前之敗，必不越魏而伐趙，校罪輕重，必不先趙而後魏，是上不上，下不下，當魏而來也。」

translations.literal: Once shamed and enraged, he is certain to employ wise strategists to devise a long plan, rely on fierce generals and drill elite troops, exert full strength in a second crossing of the river; learning from the previous defeat, he will certainly not cross Wei to attack Zhao; comparing offenses light and heavy, he will certainly not strike Zhao first and Wei afterward—the superior will neither advance nor retreat, but will come against Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and furious, he will surely turn to clever advisers for a new strategy, lean on fierce generals, and train picked troops for a full second crossing. Having learned from failure, he will not again pass through Wei to attack Zhao. Weighing who deserves punishment more, he will not hit Zhao before Wei—the court will neither advance nor retreat cleanly, but will strike directly at Wei."

sentences.zh: 季安曰：「然則若之何？」

translations.literal: Ji'an said, "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an asked, "What should we do then?"

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「王師入魏，君厚犒之。

translations.literal: Zhong said, "When the imperial army enters Wei, you should lavish rewards upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong replied, "When the court army enters Wei, treat them generously.

sentences.zh: 於是悉甲壓境，號曰伐趙，而可陰遺趙人書曰：『魏若伐趙，則河北義士謂魏賣友；

translations.literal: Then mobilize all your armor to press the border, proclaiming an attack on Zhao, but you may secretly send a letter to the Zhao people saying, 'If Wei attacks Zhao, then the righteous men of Hebei will say Wei has sold out its friend;
translations.idiomatic: Then mass your troops on the border and declare that you are marching on Zhao—but secretly send the Zhao command a letter: 'If Wei attacks Zhao, the loyal men of Hebei will say Wei has betrayed an ally;

sentences.zh: 魏若與趙，則河南忠臣謂魏反君。

translations.literal: If Wei joins with Zhao, then the loyal ministers south of the Yellow River will say Wei has turned against its sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei makes common cause with Zhao, the loyalists south of the river will call Wei rebels against the throne.

sentences.zh: 賣友反君之名，魏不忍受。

translations.literal: The names of selling friends and rebelling against the sovereign—Wei cannot bear them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cannot endure the stigma of betraying allies or turning against the emperor.

sentences.zh: 執事若能陰解陴障，遺魏一城，魏得持之奏捷天子以為符信，此乃使魏北得以奉趙，西得以為臣，於趙有角尖之耗，於魏獲不世之利，執事豈能無意於魏乎！』

translations.literal: If Your Excellency can secretly lift the defenses of a walled city and surrender one city to Wei, Wei could hold it and report victory to the Son of Heaven as proof—thus Wei could northward serve Zhao and westward be a loyal subject; for Zhao there would be a pinprick of loss, for Wei an unexampled gain—could Your Excellency be without interest in Wei!'
translations.idiomatic: If you quietly abandon one fortified town and hand it to Wei, Wei can hold it and claim a victory to the emperor as proof. Wei would thus aid Zhao to the north while remaining loyal to the court in the west. Zhao would lose only a corner of territory; Wei would gain an extraordinary prize. Surely you must have some interest in helping Wei!'

sentences.zh: 趙人脫不拒君，是魏霸基安矣。」

translations.literal: If the Zhao people do not refuse you, then Wei's foundation for hegemony will be secure.'
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao accepts, Wei's position as a dominant power will be secure.'

sentences.zh: 季安曰：「善！

translations.literal: Ji'an said, "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 先生之來，是天眷魏也。」

translations.literal: Your coming, sir, is Heaven's favor upon Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Your arrival, sir, is Heaven's blessing on Wei."

sentences.zh: 遂用忠之謀，與趙陰計，得其堂陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he employed Zhong's plan, made a secret compact with Zhao, and obtained Tangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted Tan Zhong's scheme, colluded secretly with Zhao, and secured Tangyang.

sentences.zh: 忠歸幽州，謀欲激劉濟討王承宗。

translations.literal: Zhong returned to Youzhou and plotted to incite Liu Ji to attack Wang Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong returned to Youzhou and planned to goad Liu Ji into attacking Wang Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 會濟合諸將言曰：「天子知我怨趙，今命我伐之，趙亦必大備我。

translations.literal: It happened that Ji assembled his generals and said, "The Son of Heaven knows we resent Zhao; now he orders us to attack it—Zhao is also certain to prepare heavily against us.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Ji gathered his generals and said, "The emperor knows we bear Zhao a grudge and now orders us to attack. Zhao will surely fortify heavily against us.

sentences.zh: 伐與不伐孰利？」

translations.literal: To attack or not to attack—which is more advantageous?"
translations.idiomatic: Which is better—to attack or not to attack?"

sentences.zh: 忠疾對曰：「天子終不使我伐趙，趙亦不備燕。」

translations.literal: Zhong replied swiftly, "The Son of Heaven will in the end not have us attack Zhao, and Zhao also will not prepare against Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong answered at once, "The emperor will never order us to attack Zhao, and Zhao will not prepare against Yan."

sentences.zh: 濟怒曰：「爾何不直言濟與承宗反乎！」

translations.literal: Ji flew into a rage and said, "Why do you not speak plainly that Ji and Chengzong rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji raged, "Why don't you just say openly that I am in rebellion with Chengzong!"

sentences.zh: 命系忠獄。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhong bound and put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He had Tan Zhong thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 使人視成德之境，果不為備。

translations.literal: He sent men to observe the borders of Chengde; indeed there was no preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent scouts to the Chengde frontier and found it indeed undefended.

sentences.zh: 後一日，詔果來，令濟「專護北疆，勿使朕復掛胡憂，而得專心於承宗。」

translations.literal: One day later, the edict indeed arrived, ordering Ji, "Devote yourself to guarding the northern frontier; do not let Us again be troubled by barbarian cares, so that you may concentrate on Chengzong."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the edict came as predicted, telling Liu Ji to "guard the northern border and keep barbarian troubles from reaching Us again, so that you may focus on Chengzong."

sentences.zh: 濟乃解獄召忠曰：「信如子斷矣，何以知之？」

translations.literal: Ji then released him from prison and summoned Zhong, saying, "It was truly as you judged—how did you know?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji released him and called Tan Zhong in, saying, "Your prediction was exact. How did you know?"

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「盧從史外親燕，內實忌之；

translations.literal: Zhong said, "Lu Congshi outwardly favors Yan but inwardly actually resents it;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong said, "Lu Congshi pretends friendship with Yan but secretly resents it;

sentences.zh: 外絕趙，內實與之。

translations.literal: outwardly cuts off Zhao, inwardly actually is with it.
translations.idiomatic: he publicly breaks with Zhao but secretly colludes with it.

sentences.zh: 此為趙畫曰：『燕以趙為障，雖怨趙，必不殘趙，不必為備，』一且示趙不敢抗燕，二且使燕獲疑天子。

translations.literal: For Zhao he draws up a plan saying, 'Yan uses Zhao as a barrier; though it resents Zhao, it will certainly not destroy Zhao—there is no need to prepare'—first to show Zhao dares not resist Yan, second to make Yan incur the Son of Heaven's suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He is advising Zhao: 'Yan uses Zhao as a shield; however much Yan resents Zhao, it will not crush Zhao, so you need not prepare'—partly to show Zhao need not fear Yan, partly to make the emperor suspect Yan.

sentences.zh: 趙人既不備燕，潞人則走告於天子曰：『燕厚怨趙，趙見伐而不備燕，是燕反與趙也。』

translations.literal: Since the Zhao people do not prepare against Yan, the Lu men run to tell the Son of Heaven, 'Yan deeply resents Zhao; when Zhao is attacked it does not prepare against Yan—this means Yan has turned to join Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao does not prepare against Yan, the men of Lu Province hurry to tell the emperor, 'Yan hates Zhao bitterly, yet when Zhao is under attack it does not guard against Yan—Yan must be secretly allied with Zhao.'

sentences.zh: 此所以知天子終不使君伐趙，趙亦不備燕也。」

translations.literal: From this one knows the Son of Heaven will in the end not have you attack Zhao, and Zhao also will not prepare against Yan."
translations.idiomatic: That is how I knew the emperor would never order you to attack Zhao, and Zhao would not defend against Yan."

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「今則奈何？」

translations.literal: Ji said, "Then what now?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji asked, "What should we do now?"

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「燕、趙為怨，天下無不知。

translations.literal: Zhong said, "Yan and Zhao are at odds—all under Heaven know it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong said, "The feud between Yan and Zhao is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 今天子伐趙，君坐全燕之甲，一人未濟易水，此正使潞人以燕賣恩於趙，敗忠於上，兩皆售也。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven attacks Zhao, yet you sit with all of Yan's armor without a single man crossing the Yi River—this is exactly letting the Lu men have Yan sell favor to Zhao and ruin loyalty before the sovereign; both aims are achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is attacking Zhao, yet you hold all of Yan's armies idle without a man crossing the Yi River. That only lets Lu Province paint Yan as currying favor with Zhao and disloyal to the throne—Lu wins on both counts.

sentences.zh: 是燕貯忠義之心，卒染私趙之口，不見德於趙人，惡聲徒嘈嘈於天下耳。

translations.literal: Thus Yan stores up a heart of loyalty and righteousness, yet in the end is stained with the label of privately favoring Zhao; it gains no gratitude from the Zhao people, and ill repute merely clamors throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Yan would store up loyal intent but end up branded as Zhao's secret ally—you would win no thanks from Zhao, and the realm would only hear ugly rumors.

sentences.zh: 惟君熟思之！」

translations.literal: Only let you consider this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Think this through carefully!"

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「吾知之矣。」

translations.literal: Ji said, "I understand."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji said, "I understand."

sentences.zh: 乃下令軍中曰：「五日畢出，後者醢以徇！」

translations.literal: He then issued an order to the army, "Within five days all must march out; latecomers will be minced and displayed as a warning!"
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the army, "All must depart within five days; anyone who is late will be executed and his body displayed as a warning!"
[End of speech.]"

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝上之下元和五年（

translations.literal: Below the second part of the reign account of Emperor Xianzong Zhao Wen Zhang Wu Da Sheng Zhi Shen Xiao, Yuanhe year 5 (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the annals of Emperor Xianzong, styled Zhao Wen Zhang Wu Da Sheng Zhi Shen Xiao, Yuanhe year 5 (

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公元八一零年）

translations.literal: gengyin, corresponding to the year 810 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengyin [in the sexagenary cycle], equivalent to 810 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，劉濟自將兵七萬人擊王承宗，時諸軍皆未進，濟獨前奮擊，拔饒陽、束鹿。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Liu Ji personally led seventy thousand troops to attack Wang Chengzong; at the time all the armies had not yet advanced, but Ji alone pressed forward with fierce attacks and captured Raoyang and Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Liu Ji personally led seventy thousand men against Wang Chengzong. While the other armies had not yet moved, he alone pushed forward vigorously and took Raoyang and Shulu.

sentences.zh: 河東、河中、振武、義武四軍為恆州北道招討，會於定州。

translations.literal: The four armies of Hedong, Hezhong, Zhenwu, and Yiwu served as the northern-route pacification force for Hengzhou and assembled at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong, Hezhong, Zhenwu, and Yiwu armies formed the northern-route pacification command for Hengzhou and gathered at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會望夜，軍吏以有外軍，請罷張燈。

translations.literal: On the full-moon night of the fifteenth, the army officers, because there were outside armies present, requested that lanterns not be hung.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the full moon, officers asked that festival lanterns not be lit because outside armies were present.

sentences.zh: 張茂昭曰：「三鎮，官軍也，何謂外軍！」

translations.literal: Zhang Maozhao said, "The three commands are imperial armies—what do you mean by outside armies!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhao said, "These three commands are imperial troops—what do you mean, 'outside armies'?"

sentences.zh: 命張燈，不禁行人，不閉里門，三夜如平日，亦無敢喧嘩者。

translations.literal: He ordered lanterns hung, did not forbid travelers, did not close neighborhood gates; for three nights it was as on ordinary days, and none dared make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the lanterns lit, kept the streets open and the neighborhood gates unlocked. For three nights the city was as quiet as on any ordinary day—not a soul dared cause a disturbance.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，河東將王榮拔王承宗洄湟鎮。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the Hedong general Wang Rong captured Wang Chengzong's Huihuang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Hedong general Wang Rong captured Wang Chengzong's Huihuang garrison.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀至行營，威令不振，與承宗戰，屢敗。

translations.literal: Tutu Chengcui reached the field headquarters, but his authority and orders lacked force; he fought with Chengzong and was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tutu Chengcui arrived at headquarters, but his authority carried no weight. In battle with Chengzong he suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 左神策大將軍酈定進戰死。

translations.literal: Li Dingjin, great general of the Left Divine Strategy Army, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingjin, a senior general of the Left Divine Strategy Army, was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 定進，驍將也，軍中奪氣。

translations.literal: Dingjin was a fierce general; the army lost its fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Dingjin had been a celebrated warrior, and his death broke the army's morale.

sentences.zh: 灑南尹房式有不法事，東台監察御史元稹奏攝之，擅令停務。

translations.literal: The Governor of Weinan, Fang Shi, had unlawful affairs; the Eastern Platform investigating censor Yuan Zhen memorialized to take over his duties and on his own authority ordered work suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fang Shi of Weinan was accused of misconduct. Investigating censor Yuan Zhen of the Eastern Platform petitioned to take over his office and on his own authority ordered official business halted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為不可，罰一季俸，召還西京。

translations.literal: The court regarded this as impermissible, fined him one season's salary, and recalled him to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled this improper, docked him a quarter-year's salary, and ordered him back to the western capital.

sentences.zh: 至敷水驛，有內侍後至，破驛門呼罵而入，以馬鞭擊稹傷面。

translations.literal: When he reached Fushui post station, an inner attendant arrived later, broke the post gate, entered shouting curses, and struck Zhen's face with a riding crop, wounding him.
translations.idiomatic: At Fushui post station a palace eunuch arrived after him, broke down the gate, burst in cursing, and whipped Yuan Zhen across the face.

sentences.zh: 上復引稹前過，貶江陵士曹。

translations.literal: The emperor again cited Zhen's previous faults and demoted him to army corps assistant in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again invoked Yuan Zhen's earlier offenses and demoted him to staff officer in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李絳、崔群言稹無罪。

translations.literal: The Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Cui Qun said Zhen was without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Cui Qun argued that Yuan Zhen was innocent.

sentences.zh: 白居易上言：「中使陵辱朝士，中使不問而稹先貶，恐自今中使出外益暴橫，人無敢言者。

translations.literal: Bai Juyi submitted a memorial, saying, "The inner attendant insulted and humiliated a court official; the inner attendant was not questioned yet Zhen was first demoted—I fear from now on when inner attendants go out they will become still more violent and overbearing, and none will dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi memorialized the throne: "A eunuch publicly humiliated a court official, yet the eunuch goes unpunished while Yuan Zhen is punished first. From now on eunuchs on provincial duty will grow even more brutal, and no one will dare speak out.

sentences.zh: 又，稹為御史，多所舉奏，不避權勢，切齒者眾，恐自今無人肯為陛下當官執法，疾惡繩愆，有大奸猾，陛下無從得知。」

translations.literal: Moreover, as censor Zhen impeached many cases and did not avoid powerful interests; those who gnashed their teeth at him were many—I fear from now on none will be willing to serve Your Majesty in office and enforce the law, hate evil and punish faults, and when there are great villains and schemers, Your Majesty will have no means to learn of them."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as a censor Yuan Zhen impeached many powerful men without fear. His enemies are legion. I fear that from now on no one will enforce the law for Your Majesty or root out corruption—and when great villains plot, Your Majesty will never hear of it."

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to heed them.

sentences.zh: 上以河朔方用兵，不能討吳少陽。

translations.literal: Because the emperor was employing troops in the Hebei region, he could not attack Wu Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because campaigns were already underway in Hebei, the emperor could not move against Wu Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，己未，以少陽為淮西留後。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiwei, Shaoyang was appointed acting military governor of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiwei, Shaoyang was confirmed as acting military governor of Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 諸軍討王承宗者久無功，白居易上言，以為：「河北本不當用兵，今既出師，承璀未嘗苦戰，已失大將，與從史兩軍入賊境，遷延進退，不惟意在逗留，亦是力難支敵。

translations.literal: The armies attacking Wang Chengzong for a long time had no success; Bai Juyi submitted a memorial, holding that: "Hebei originally ought not to have been attacked with troops; now that armies have been sent, Chengcui has never fought bitter battles yet has already lost a great general; together with Congshi's two armies entering rebel territory, they delay advancing and retreating—not only do their intentions lie in stalling, but they also find it hard to withstand the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign against Wang Chengzong had dragged on without success. Bai Juyi submitted a memorial arguing that military action in Hebei had been a mistake from the start. Tutu Chengcui had not fought hard yet had already lost a senior general. Lu Congshi's forces, like his own, had entered rebel territory but lingered—in part by design, in part because they could not overcome the enemy.

sentences.zh: 希朝、茂昭至新市鎮，竟不能過。

translations.literal: Xichao and Maozhao reached Xinshi garrison but in the end could not pass it.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao and Maozhao reached Xinshi but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 劉濟引全軍攻圍樂壽，久不能下。

translations.literal: Liu Ji led his entire army to attack and besiege Leshou but for a long time could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji brought his full army to besiege Leshou but could not capture it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 師道、季安元不可保，察其情狀，似相計會，各收一縣，遂不進軍。

translations.literal: Shidao and Ji'an originally could not be relied upon; observing their conduct, they seemed to have coordinated plans, each taking one county, and then ceasing to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao and Ji'an were never trustworthy; they appear to have colluded, each seizing a single county and then refusing to advance further.

sentences.zh: 陛下觀此事勢，成功有何所望！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, look at the trend of this affair—what hope is there of success!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should look at how matters stand—what hope is there of victory?

sentences.zh: 以臣愚見，須速罷兵，若又遲疑，其害有四：可為痛惜者二，可為深憂者二。

translations.literal: In this subject's foolish view, troops must quickly be withdrawn; if there is further delay, the harms are four: two that may cause grief, two that may cause deep worry.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, you must withdraw the armies at once. Further hesitation brings four kinds of harm—two deeply regrettable, two deeply alarming.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 若保有成，即不論用度多少；

translations.literal: If success is assured, then one need not consider how much expense;
translations.idiomatic: If victory were assured, cost would not matter;

sentences.zh: 既的知不可，即不合虛費貲糧。

translations.literal: since it is already clearly known to be impossible, then one ought not wastefully spend funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: but when defeat is clearly inevitable, it is wrong to squander treasury and supplies.

sentences.zh: 悟而後行，事亦非晚。

translations.literal: To act after understanding is still not too late.
translations.idiomatic: Acting once you see the truth is still not too late.

sentences.zh: 今遲校一日有一日之費，更延旬月，所費滋多，終須罷兵，何如早罷！

translations.literal: Now each day of delay costs a day's expense; extend it by ten days or a month and the cost grows ever greater—you must end up withdrawing the armies, so why not withdraw early!
translations.idiomatic: Every day of delay adds a day's expense. Stretch it out another month and the waste only grows. You will have to withdraw eventually—why not do it now?

sentences.zh: 以府庫錢帛、百姓脂膏資助河北諸侯，轉令強大。

translations.literal: Using treasury money and silk and the fat and marrow of the people to subsidize the Hebei feudal lords will in turn make them stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury funds and the people's taxed labor are enriching the Hebei warlords and making them stronger.

sentences.zh: 此臣為陛下痛惜者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter for which this subject grieves on Your Majesty's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: That is my first reason for grief on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 臣又恐河北諸將見吳少陽已受制命，必引事例輕重，同詞請雪承宗。

translations.literal: This subject further fears that when the Hebei generals see Wu Shaoyang has already received an imperial appointment, they will surely cite precedents comparing light and heavy cases and with one voice petition to clear Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: I also fear that when the Hebei generals see Wu Shaoyang confirmed in office, they will cite his precedent and jointly petition to pardon Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 若章表繼來，即義無不許。

translations.literal: If memorials come in succession, then on principle none can be refused.
translations.idiomatic: If such petitions arrive one after another, you will have no honorable way to refuse.

sentences.zh: 請而後捨，體勢可知，轉令承宗膠固同類。

translations.literal: To petition and then abandon the campaign—the posture is predictable; it will in turn make Chengzong stick fast with his kind.
translations.idiomatic: Granting requests only after dragging your feet will show everyone your weakness and bind Chengzong more tightly to his allies.

sentences.zh: 如此，則與奪皆由鄰道，恩信不出朝廷，實恐威權盡歸河北。

translations.literal: Thus, granting and withholding would all depend on neighboring commands; favor and trust would not come from the court—I truly fear authority would entirely pass to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment would then rest with neighboring commands, not the throne. Imperial grace and authority would drain entirely into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 此為陛下痛惜者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second matter for which one grieves on Your Majesty's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: That is my second reason for grief.

sentences.zh: 今天時已熱，兵氣相蒸，至於飢渴疲勞，疾疫暴露，驅以就戰，人何以堪！

translations.literal: Now the season is already hot, martial energy steams together; as for hunger, thirst, fatigue, pestilence, and exposure—driven to battle, how can men endure!
translations.idiomatic: The weather is already hot; the army stewing in camp suffers hunger, thirst, exhaustion, disease, and exposure. How can soldiers be driven into battle under such conditions?

sentences.zh: 縱不惜身，亦難忍苦。

translations.literal: Even if they do not value their lives, they can hardly bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Even men who do not fear death can scarcely endure such hardship.

sentences.zh: 況神策烏雜城市之人，例皆不慣如此，忽思生路，或有奔逃，一人若逃，百人相扇，一軍若散，諸軍必搖，事忽至此，悔將何及！

translations.literal: Moreover, the Divine Strategy troops are a mixed rabble of city dwellers, who by rule are all unaccustomed to such things; suddenly thinking of a way to live, some may flee—if one man flees, a hundred will fan the flames; if one army scatters, all armies will be shaken; if matters suddenly reach this point, regret will be too late!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Divine Strategy Army is largely drawn from city men unaccustomed to hardship. At the first thought of escape, some will run. One deserter will stir a hundred; one routed army will shake them all. If things reach that point, it will be too late for regret!

sentences.zh: 此為陛下深憂者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter of deep worry for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: That is my first deep alarm.

sentences.zh: 臣聞回鶻、吐蕃皆有細作，中國之事，小大盡知。

translations.literal: This subject has heard that both the Uyghurs and the Tibetans have spies; affairs of China, great and small, they know entirely.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that both the Uyghurs and Tibetans maintain spies who learn everything that happens in China, great and small.

sentences.zh: 今聚天下之兵，唯討承宗一賊，自冬及夏，都未立功，則兵力之強弱，資費之多少，豈宜使西戌、北虜一一知之！

translations.literal: Now gathering the armies of the empire to attack only the one rebel Chengzong, from winter until summer achieving no merit—the strong and weak of military force, the much and little of supplies—ought these be let the western garrisons and northern barbarians know one by one!
translations.idiomatic: The empire has massed its armies against a single rebel, Wang Chengzong, yet from winter through summer has won nothing. Should our weakness, our costs, and our failures be laid bare for every western garrison and northern barbarian to see?

sentences.zh: 忽見利生心，乘虛入寇，以今日之勢力，可能救其首尾哉！

translations.literal: Suddenly seeing profit, they take heart and exploit the void to invade—with today's strength, can both ends be saved!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing their opening, they may invade—and with our forces in their present state, how could we defend both frontiers at once?

sentences.zh: 兵連禍生，何事不有！

translations.literal: When armies connect, calamities arise—what might not happen!
translations.idiomatic: When war drags on, disasters multiply—anything becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 萬一及此，實關安危。

translations.literal: If by chance it reaches this point, it truly bears on safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Should that come to pass, the fate of the realm would hang in the balance.

sentences.zh: 此其為陛下深憂者二也。」

translations.literal: This is the second deep worry for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: That is my second deep alarm.
[End of memorial.]"

sentences.zh: 盧從史首建伐王承宗之謀，及朝廷興師，從史逗留不進，陰與承宗通謀，令軍士潛懷承宗號；

translations.literal: Lu Congshi was the first to propose the plan to attack Wang Chengzong; when the court raised armies, Congshi lingered without advancing, secretly communicated plans with Chengzong, and had soldiers secretly carry Chengzong's tally;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi had first urged the campaign against Wang Chengzong. Once the court mobilized, however, he stalled and secretly colluded with Chengzong, ordering his soldiers to carry Chengzong's battle tokens in secret;

sentences.zh: 又高芻粟之價以敗度支，諷朝廷求平章事，誣奏諸道與賊通，不可進兵，上甚患之。

translations.literal: He also raised the price of fodder and grain to ruin the Directorate of Public Works, hinted to the court that he be made chief minister, and falsely memorialized that the various commands were in communication with the rebels and that troops should not advance—the emperor was greatly troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: He also inflated fodder prices to wreck the budget bureau, hinted that he should be made chief minister, and falsely reported that other commands were colluding with the rebels and that the army should not advance. The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 會從史遣牙將王翊元入奏事，裴垍引與語，為言為臣之義，微動其心，翊元遂輸誠，言從史陰謀及可取之狀。

translations.literal: At the same time Congshi sent his staff officer Wang Yiyuan to the capital to report affairs; Pei Ji led him into conversation, speaking on the duty of a subject, subtly stirring his heart; Yiyuan then pledged sincerity and spoke of Congshi's secret plots and the condition in which he could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Lu Congshi dispatched his staff officer Wang Yiyuan to court on routine business. Pei Ji drew him into conversation and spoke movingly of a subject's duties, gently swaying him. Wang then opened his heart, revealing Congshi's secret machinations and how the man might be seized.

sentences.zh: 垍令翊元還本軍經營，復來京師，遂得其都知兵馬使烏重胤等款要。

translations.literal: Ji ordered Yiyuan to return to his original army to manage affairs, then come again to the capital; thus he secured the secret goodwill of the army commanders of military affairs Wu Chongyin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji sent Wang back to the army to lay groundwork, then return to the capital again. Through this he won over the commander of military affairs Wu Chongyin and other key officers.

sentences.zh: 垍言於上曰：「從史狡猾驕很，必將為亂。

translations.literal: Ji spoke to the emperor, saying: "Congshi is crafty, arrogant, and fierce—he will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji told the emperor, "Congshi is cunning, arrogant, and truculent. He is bound to revolt.

sentences.zh: 今聞其與承璀對營，視承璀如嬰兒，往來殊不設備。

translations.literal: Now I hear that he camps opposite Chenghuan and treats Chenghuan like an infant; in coming and going he sets no guard at all.
translations.idiomatic: I hear he is encamped face to face with Chenghuan and treats him like a child. He comes and goes with almost no precaution.

sentences.zh: 失今不取，後雖興大兵，未可以歲月平也。」

translations.literal: If we miss the chance now and do not take him, afterward even if we raise a great army, it cannot be pacified within months and years."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to strike now, even a major campaign later may not subdue him within years.

sentences.zh: 上初愕然，熟思良久，乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor at first was startled, pondered deeply for a long while, and then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken aback at first. After long reflection he agreed.

sentences.zh: 從史性貪，承璀盛陳奇玩，視其所欲，稍以遺之。

translations.literal: Congshi's nature was greedy; Chenghuan abundantly displayed rare curios, watched what he desired, and gradually gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi was greedy by nature. Chenghuan laid out rare treasures, noted what caught his eye, and gradually sent them as gifts.

sentences.zh: 從史喜，益相暱狎。

translations.literal: Congshi was pleased and grew even more intimate and familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Congshi grew ever closer and more at ease with him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，承璀與行營兵馬使李聽謀，召從史入營博，伏壯士於幕下，突出，擒詣帳後縛之，內車中，馳詣京師。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Chenghuan and the field-army commander of military affairs Li Ting plotted; they summoned Congshi into camp to gamble, hid strong men beneath the tent curtain; they burst forth, seized him, took him behind the tent and bound him, put him inside a carriage, and galloped to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Chenghuan and field commander Li Ting laid a trap. They invited Congshi into camp for a game of chance, with braves hidden beneath the tent. When the moment came they sprang out, seized him, bound him behind the pavilion, shut him in a carriage, and raced for the capital.

sentences.zh: 左右驚亂，承璀斬十餘人，諭以詔旨。

translations.literal: Those around were alarmed and in disorder; Chenghuan executed more than ten men and announced the edict's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi's attendants panicked. Chenghuan cut down more than ten men and proclaimed the imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 從史營中士卒聞之，皆甲以出，操兵趨嘩。

translations.literal: Soldiers in Congshi's camp, hearing this, all donned armor and came out, grasping weapons and rushing forward clamorously.
translations.idiomatic: When the soldiers in Congshi's camp heard what had happened, they armored and poured out, weapons in hand, shouting as they surged forward.

sentences.zh: 烏重胤當軍門叱之曰：「天子有詔，從者賞，敢違者斬！」

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin stood at the camp gate and shouted at them: "The Son of Heaven has an edict—those who follow will be rewarded; those who dare disobey will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin planted himself at the gate and bellowed, "The Son of Heaven has issued an edict! Follow it and be rewarded; defy it and die!

sentences.zh: 士卒皆斂兵還部伍。

translations.literal: The soldiers all sheathed their weapons and returned to their units.
translations.idiomatic: The troops lowered their weapons and fell back into ranks.

sentences.zh: 會夜，車疾驅，未明，已出境。

translations.literal: It happened to be night; the carriage drove swiftly, and before dawn had already crossed the border.
translations.idiomatic: That night the carriage raced on through the darkness. Before dawn it was already beyond Zhaoyi territory.

sentences.zh: 重胤，承洽之子；

translations.literal: Chongyin was the son of Cheng He;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin was the son of Cheng He;

sentences.zh: 聽，晟之子也。

translations.literal: Ting was the son of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting was the son of Li Sheng.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，范希朝、張茂昭大破承宗之眾於木刀溝。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Fan Xichao and Zhang Maozhao greatly defeated Chengzong's forces at Mudao Gully.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Fan Xichao and Zhang Maozhao routed Wang Chengzong's army at Mudao Gully.

sentences.zh: 上嘉烏重胤之功，欲即授以昭義節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Wu Chongyin's achievement and wished immediately to appoint him military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor applauded Wu Chongyin's role in the arrest and wished to appoint him governor of Zhaoyi at once.

sentences.zh: 李絳以為不可，請授重胤河陽，以河陽節度使孟元陽鎮昭義。

translations.literal: Li Jiang held it impossible and requested that Chongyin be given Heyang, and that Heyang military governor Meng Yuanyang be stationed over Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang objected. He urged that Chongyin receive Heyang instead, with Heyang governor Meng Yuanyang sent to govern Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 會吐突承璀奏，已牒重胤句當昭義留後，絳上言：「昭義五州據山東要害，魏博、恆、幽諸鎮蟠結，朝廷恃此以制之。

translations.literal: It happened that Tuyu Chenghuan memorialized that he had already issued a document appointing Chongyin to manage Zhaoyi as acting governor; Jiang submitted: "The five prefectures of Zhaoyi occupy the strategic passes east of the mountains; the commands of Weibo, Heng, and You are intertwined like coiled serpents; the court relies on this to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Tuyu Chenghuan reported that he had already ordered Wu Chongyin to serve as acting governor of Zhaoyi. Li Jiang memorialized: "Zhaoyi's five prefectures hold the vital passes of the eastern provinces. Weibo, Hengzhou, and Youzhou are tangled in mutual dependence, and the court relies on Zhaoyi to keep them in check.

sentences.zh: 邢、滋、洺入其腹內，誠國之寶地，安危所繫也。

translations.literal: Xing, Zi, and Luo lie within its belly—they are truly the treasured lands of the state, on which safety and peril depend.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, Zi, and Luo lie at its heart—the very jewel of the realm, and a pivot of national security.

sentences.zh: 向為從史所據，使朝廷旰食，今幸而得之，承璀復以與重胤，臣聞之驚歎，實所痛心！

translations.literal: Formerly occupied by Congshi, it made the court eat late in the evening; now, having fortunately regained it, Chenghuan again gives it to Chongyin—I hear this with alarm and sigh; it truly grieves the heart!
translations.idiomatic: Congshi's hold on it once kept the court sleepless with worry. We have only just regained it, and now Chenghuan would hand it to Chongyin. I am appalled—this cuts to the bone!

sentences.zh: 昨國家誘執從史，雖為長策，已失大體。

translations.literal: Yesterday the state lured and seized Congshi—though a far-reaching stratagem, it already lost the larger propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday's scheme to lure and capture Congshi, however wise as tactics, already compromised the court's dignity.

sentences.zh: 今承璀又以文牒差人為重鎮留後，為之求旌節，無君之心，孰甚於此！

translations.literal: Now Chenghuan again uses an official document to appoint someone as acting governor of a great command and seeks a commission and banner for him—disloyalty to the ruler, what exceeds this!
translations.idiomatic: Now Chenghuan would use a mere dispatch to install his man over a great command and petition for the commission of office for him. What greater sign of contempt for imperial authority could there be?

sentences.zh: 陛下昨日得昭義，人神同慶，威令再立；

translations.literal: Your Majesty yesterday gained Zhaoyi—human and divine alike rejoiced, and imperial authority was re-established;
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Your Majesty recovered Zhaoyi, heaven and earth rejoiced, and imperial prestige was restored.

sentences.zh: 今日忽以授本軍牙將，物情頓沮，紀綱大紊。

translations.literal: Today suddenly giving it to this army's staff officer—public sentiment is instantly dejected, and discipline is greatly disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Today you would suddenly award it to a mere staff officer of the garrison. Morale will collapse and order will unravel.

sentences.zh: 校計利害，更不若從史為之。

translations.literal: Weighing advantage and harm, it would be less bad to leave Congshi in charge.
translations.idiomatic: On balance, even Congshi would have been preferable.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 從史雖蓄奸謀，已是朝廷牧伯。

translations.literal: Congshi, though harboring treacherous designs, was already the court's territorial lord.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi, for all his scheming, had already been a recognized regional governor appointed by the throne.

sentences.zh: 重胤出於列校，以承璀一牒代之，竊恐河南、北諸侯聞之，無不憤怒，恥與為伍。
