translations.literal: Chongyin came from the ranks of commanders; to replace him with a single document from Chenghuan—I privately fear that when the feudal lords north and south of the Yellow River hear this, none will fail to rage with anger and deem it shameful to be ranked with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin rose from the ranks of junior officers. To replace a governor with one slip from Chenghuan—I fear every warlord north and south of the Yellow River will erupt in fury and count it shameful to stand his equal.

sentences.zh: 且謂承璀誘重胤使逐從史而代其位，彼人人麾下各有將校，能無自危乎！

translations.literal: Moreover they will say Chenghuan tempted Chongyin to drive out Congshi and take his place—in each man's command there are generals and officers of his own; how can they not feel peril to themselves!
translations.idiomatic: They will say Chenghuan induced Chongyin to oust Congshi and seize his post. Every commander has his own officers—would they not fear the same fate?

sentences.zh: 儻劉濟、茂昭、季安、執恭、韓弘、師道繼有章表陳其情狀，並指承璀專命之罪，不知陛下何以處之？

translations.literal: If Liu Ji, Maozhao, Ji'an, Zhigong, Han Hong, and Shidao successively submit memorials stating their grievances, all pointing to Chenghuan's crime of acting on his own authority—Your Majesty will not know how to deal with it?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Liu Ji, Zhang Maozhao, Li Ji'an, Tian Zhigong, Han Hong, and Li Shidao follow with memorials laying out their grievances and accusing Chenghuan of usurping imperial authority—how will Your Majesty answer?

sentences.zh: 若皆不報，則眾怒益甚；

translations.literal: If none are answered, then public wrath will grow all the more;
translations.idiomatic: Ignore them all, and the outrage will only deepen.

sentences.zh: 若為之改除，則朝廷之威重去矣。」

translations.literal: If appointments are changed for them, then the court's majesty and authority are lost."
translations.idiomatic: Yield to their demands, and the court's authority is spent.

sentences.zh: 上復使樞密使梁守謙密謀於絳曰：「今重胤已總軍務，事不得已，須應與節。」

translations.literal: The emperor again had Privy Council commissioner Liang Shouqian secretly consult Jiang, saying: "Now Chongyin already holds overall military affairs; the matter is unavoidable—we must grant him the commission."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Privy Council commissioner Liang Shouqian to consult Li Jiang in secret. "Chongyin already commands the army. The situation leaves no choice—we must give him the commission.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「從史為帥不由朝廷，故啟其邪心，終成逆節。

translations.literal: He replied: "Congshi became commander not through the court—therefore his evil heart was opened, and he finally became a traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang answered, "Congshi became commander without court approval. That fed his ambitions until he turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 今以重胤典兵，即授之節，威福之柄不在朝廷，何以異於從史乎！

translations.literal: Now making Chongyin hold the army and immediately granting him the commission—the handle of authority and blessing is not in the court's hands—how is this different from Congshi!
translations.idiomatic: Grant Chongyin command of the army and immediately confirm him in office, and the source of power no longer rests with the court. How is that different from Congshi?

sentences.zh: 重胤之得河陽，已為望外之福，豈敢更為旅拒！

translations.literal: Chongyin's gaining Heyang is already a blessing beyond expectation—how would he dare further to resist as a stranger!
translations.idiomatic: For Chongyin, Heyang alone would be reward beyond his dreams. He would hardly dare refuse it!

sentences.zh: 況重胤所以能執從史，本以杖順成功，一旦自逆詔命，安知同列不襲其跡而動乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason Chongyin could seize Congshi was originally by wielding obedience to succeed; once he himself goes against the edict, who knows whether his peers will not follow his own example and act!
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin seized Congshi by obeying the throne. If he now defies an imperial order, what is to stop his fellow officers from doing to him what he did to Congshi?

sentences.zh: 重胤軍中等夷甚多，必不願重胤獨為主帥。

translations.literal: In Chongyin's army there are many of equal rank—they surely will not wish Chongyin alone to be chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: Many in his army are his equals in rank. They will not welcome his elevation above them alone.

sentences.zh: 移之他鎮，乃愜眾心，何憂其致亂乎！」

translations.literal: Transfer him to another command—that satisfies the multitude's hearts; why worry that he will bring disorder!"
translations.idiomatic: Transfer him to another command and you satisfy the troops. What risk of disorder remains?

sentences.zh: 上悅，皆如其請。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and did all as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was persuaded and granted everything Li Jiang asked.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以重胤為河陽節度使，元陽為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: On renchen, Chongyin was made military governor of Heyang and Yuanyang military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wu Chongyin was appointed governor of Heyang and Meng Yuanyang governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，貶盧從史歡州司馬。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Lu Congshi was demoted to prefectural aide of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Lu Congshi was banished to serve as deputy prefect of Huan.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙巳，昭義軍三千餘人夜潰，奔魏州。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on yisi, more than three thousand men of the Zhaoyi army fled by night in rout, running to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yisi, more than three thousand Zhaoyi troops broke and fled by night toward Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 劉濟奏拔安平。

translations.literal: Liu Ji memorialized that Anping had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji reported the capture of Anping.

sentences.zh: 庚申，吐蕃遣其臣論思邪熱入見，且歸路泌、鄭叔矩之柩。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Tibet sent its minister Lun Siyexie to enter audience and also return the coffins of Lu Bi and Zheng Shuju.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Tibet sent the minister Lun Siyexie to audience, bearing also the remains of Lu Bi and Zheng Shuju for repatriation.

sentences.zh: 甲子，奚寇靈州。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Xi raided Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Xi tribesmen raided Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲申，白居易復上奏，以為：「臣比請罷兵，今之事勢，又不如前，不知陛下復何所待！」

translations.literal: Sixth month, on jiashen, Bai Juyi again submitted a memorial, stating: "Your subject recently requested cessation of troops; the present situation is again worse than before—I do not know what Your Majesty is still waiting for!"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiashen, Bai Juyi memorialized again: "I recently urged you to end the war. Affairs are now worse than before. What further delay does Your Majesty await?

sentences.zh: 是時，上每有軍國大事，必與諸學士謀之。

translations.literal: At this time, whenever the emperor had great affairs of state and army, he necessarily deliberated on them with the various academicians.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor routinely consulted his Hanlin academicians on every major military and political decision.

sentences.zh: 嘗逾月不見學士，李絳等上言：「臣等飽食不言，其自為計則得矣，如陛下何！

translations.literal: Once, for more than a month the emperor did not see the academicians. Li Jiang and others submitted a memorial saying: "We eat our fill and do not speak; as a plan for ourselves it would suffice, but what of Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the emperor went more than a month without summoning his academicians. Li Jiang and the others memorialized: "We may eat in idleness and hold our tongues—that may serve our private interests, but what of Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 陛下詢訪理道，開納直言，實天下之幸，豈臣等之幸！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty inquires about governing principles and opens the way to frank speech—truly this is the fortune of the empire; how could it be the fortune of your servants!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks out the Way of governance and welcomes honest counsel. That is truly the empire's good fortune—not merely our own."

sentences.zh: 上遽令「明日三殿對來。」

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered: "Come for an audience in the Three Halls tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once commanded: "Present yourselves for audience in the Three Halls tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 白居易嘗因論事，言「陛下錯」，上色莊而罷，密召承旨李絳，謂：「白居易小臣不遜，須令出院。」

translations.literal: Bai Juyi once, in discussing affairs, said "Your Majesty is wrong." The emperor's countenance grew stern and the session ended. He secretly summoned Chief Drafter Li Jiang and said: "Bai Juyi, a petty official, is insolent—I must have him dismissed from the Academy."
translations.idiomatic: During a policy debate, Bai Juyi once declared, "Your Majesty is mistaken." The emperor's face darkened and the session ended. Privately he summoned Chief Academician Li Jiang and said: "That presumptuous minor official Bai Juyi must be removed from the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「陛下容納直言，故群臣敢竭誠無隱。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Your Majesty tolerates frank speech; therefore the ministers dare to exhaust their sincerity and hold nothing back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang replied: "Your Majesty has been willing to hear blunt counsel. That is why the ministers dare speak their minds without concealment.

sentences.zh: 居易言雖少思，志在納忠。

translations.literal: Though Bai Juyi's words lacked some reflection, his intent was to offer loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi's remark was hasty, but his purpose was loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 陛下今日罪之，臣恐天下各思箝口，非所以廣聰明，昭聖德也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty today punishes him, I fear that throughout the empire all will think to seal their mouths—this is not the means to extend discernment and manifest sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: If you punish him now, I fear men everywhere will think twice before speaking. That would not enlarge your wisdom or display your sage virtue."

sentences.zh: 上悅，待居易如初。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and treated Bai Juyi as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was mollified and continued to treat Bai Juyi as he had before.

sentences.zh: 上嘗欲近獵苑中，至蓬萊池西，謂左右曰：「李絳必諫，不如且止。」

translations.literal: The emperor once wished to hunt close within the imperial park. When he reached the west of Penglai Pool, he said to those around him: "Li Jiang is sure to remonstrate—better to stop for now."
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor planned to hunt near the palace grounds. Reaching the west side of Penglai Pool, he told his attendants: "Li Jiang is bound to object—we had better turn back for now."
[End of speech.]"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，王承宗遣使自陳為盧從史所離間，乞輸貢賦，請官吏，許其自新。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gengzi, Wang Chengzong sent an envoy to state on his own behalf that he had been estranged by Lu Congshi, begging to submit tribute and taxes and requesting officials, asking permission to reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, Wang Chengzong dispatched envoys to explain that Lu Congshi had turned him against the court. He offered to resume paying tribute and taxes, requested the appointment of imperial officials, and asked to be allowed to return to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 李師道等數上表請雪承宗，朝廷亦以師久無功，丁未，制洗雪承宗，以為成德軍節度使，復以德、棣二州與之。

translations.literal: Li Shidao and others repeatedly submitted memorials asking to clear Wang Chengzong's name. The court also, because the campaign had long been without success, on dingwei issued an edict clearing Chengzong, appointing him military governor of Chengde, and restored to him the two prefectures of De and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao and others memorialized repeatedly asking that Wang Chengzong be rehabilitated. The court, weary of a campaign that had dragged on without victory, on dingwei issued an edict clearing Chengzong's name, restored him as military governor of Chengde, and returned De and Di prefectures to his control.

sentences.zh: 悉罷諸道行營將士，共賜布帛二十八萬端匹，加劉濟中書令。

translations.literal: All campaigning troops from the various circuits were entirely dismissed. In all, two hundred eighty thousand bolts of cloth and silk were bestowed, and Liu Ji was promoted to Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: The campaigning forces from every circuit were disbanded. The troops were collectively rewarded with 280,000 bolts of cloth and silk, and Liu Ji was given the additional title of Palace Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 劉濟之討王承宗也，以長子緄為副大使，掌幽州留務。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji was campaigning against Wang Chengzong, he made his eldest son Kun vice commissioner and put him in charge of administrative affairs left behind at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Ji was fighting Wang Chengzong, he left his eldest son Kun as deputy commissioner to manage affairs at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 濟軍瀛州，次子總為瀛州刺史，濟署行營都知兵馬使，使屯饒陽。

translations.literal: Ji encamped at Yingzhou. His second son Zong was Yingzhou prefect. Ji appointed him campaigning army chief controller of military affairs and had him garrison at Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji kept his army at Ying Prefecture, where his second son Zong served as prefect. Ji named Zong chief controller of military affairs for the campaigning army and stationed him at Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 濟有疾，總與判官張玘、孔目官成國寶謀，詐使人從長安來，曰：「朝廷以相公逗留無功，已除副大使為節度使矣。」

translations.literal: When Ji fell ill, Zong conspired with aide Zhang Qi and chief clerk Cheng Guobao. They falsely sent a man from Chang'an saying: "The court, because the chief minister has lingered without achievement, has already removed the vice commissioner and made him military governor."
translations.idiomatic: When Ji fell sick, Zong plotted with his staff officer Zhang Qi and chief clerk Cheng Guobao. They sent a man falsely claiming to have come from Chang'an, who announced: "Because you have stalled without success, the court has already replaced your vice commissioner and made him military governor."

sentences.zh: 明日，又使人來告曰：「副大使旌節已至太原。」

translations.literal: The next day another man was sent to report: "The vice commissioner's banners and batons of authority have already reached Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The next day another messenger arrived saying the vice commissioner's commission insignia had already reached Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 又使人走而呼曰：「旌節已過代州。」

translations.literal: Again a man was sent running to shout: "The banners and batons have already passed Daizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Still another runner was sent to cry out that the commission insignia had already passed Daizhou."

sentences.zh: 舉軍驚駭。

translations.literal: The whole army was startled and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 濟憤怒不知所為，殺大將素與緄厚者數十人，追緄詣行營，以張玘兄皋代知留務。

translations.literal: Ji, enraged and not knowing what to do, killed several dozen senior generals who had always been close to Kun, pursued Kun to the campaigning encampment, and had Zhang Qi's elder brother Gao replace him in charge of the affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, furious and at a loss, executed several dozen senior commanders who had long been close to Kun, then rode after Kun toward the campaigning army's headquarters. He put Zhang Qi's elder brother Gao in charge of affairs at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 濟自朝至日昃不食，渴索飲，總因置毒而進之。

translations.literal: From morning until the sun slanted westward Ji ate nothing. Thirsty, he asked for drink; Zong had poison placed in it and brought it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji took no food from morning until midafternoon. When thirst drove him to ask for water, Zong had it poisoned and served it himself.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，濟薨。

translations.literal: On yimao, Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Liu Ji died.

sentences.zh: 緄行至涿州，總矯以父命杖殺之，遂領軍務。

translations.literal: As Kun was traveling and reached Zhuozhou, Zong forged his father's command and had him beaten to death with staves, then took over military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Kun reached Zhu Prefecture, Zong forged his father's order and had him clubbed to death, then assumed command of the army.

sentences.zh: 嶺南監軍許遂振以飛語毀節度使楊於陵於上，上命召於陵還，除冗官。

translations.literal: Xu Suizhen, the army supervisor of Lingnan, used rumors to slander Military Governor Yang Yuling before the emperor. The emperor ordered Yang Yuling recalled and assigned him a supernumerary post.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Suizhen, the eunuch army supervisor in Lingnan, whispered slanders against Yang Yuling to the throne. The emperor summoned Yang back to court and relegated him to a nominal office.

sentences.zh: 裴垍曰：「於陵性廉直，陛下以遂振故黜籓臣，不可。」

translations.literal: Pei Ji said: "Yuling's nature is honest and upright. Your Majesty, because of Suizhen, would dismiss a frontier minister—this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji objected: "Yang Yuling is a man of integrity. You must not remove a frontier governor merely on Xu Suizhen's word."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以於陵為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Yang Yuling was made Vice Minister of the Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Yang Yuling was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遂振尋自抵罪。

translations.literal: Suizhen before long brought guilt upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu Suizhen was himself found guilty.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥，上與宰相語及神仙，問：「果有之乎？」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yihai, the emperor spoke with the chief ministers about immortals and asked: "Do they really exist?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yihai, the emperor asked his chief ministers about immortals: "Are such beings real?"

sentences.zh: 李籓對曰：「秦始皇、漢武帝學仙之效，具載前史，太宗服天竺僧長年藥致疾，此古今之明戒也。

translations.literal: Li Fan answered: "The results of Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han in studying immortality are fully recorded in former histories. Emperor Taizong took the longevity medicine of the Tianzhu monk and fell ill—this is a clear warning of ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan replied: "Earlier histories record in full what came of Qin Shihuang's and Han Wudi's pursuit of immortality. Emperor Taizong grew ill after taking a longevity elixir from an Indian monk. That is a warning every age should heed.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋鼎盛，方勵志太平，宜拒絕方士之說。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years are in full prime; you are just now striving in aspiration for the Great Peace—you should reject the talk of sorcerers.
translations.idiomatic: You are still in the prime of life and striving to bring the realm to peace. You should reject the claims of occult practitioners.

sentences.zh: 苟道盛德充，人安國理，何憂無堯、舜之壽乎！」

translations.literal: If the Way flourishes and virtue is fulfilled, the people are at peace and the state is well governed—why worry about not having the long life of Yao and Shun!"
translations.idiomatic: If your virtue is complete and the people live in peace under just governance, why should you fear falling short of the longevity of Yao and Shun!"
[End of memorial.]"

sentences.zh: 九月，己亥，吐突承璀自行營還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jihai, TuTu Chenghuan returned from the campaigning encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jihai, TuTu Chenghuan came back from the front.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，復為左衛上將軍，充左軍中尉。

translations.literal: On xinhai, he was again made Left Guard General-in-Chief and served as Left Army Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he was restored as Left Guard General-in-Chief and reappointed Left Army Inner Attendant.

sentences.zh: 裴垍曰：「承璀首唱用兵，疲弊天下，卒無成功，陛下縱以舊恩不加顯戮，豈得全不貶黜以謝天下乎！」

translations.literal: Pei Ji said: "Chenghuan was the first to advocate using troops; he exhausted and impoverished the empire, and in the end achieved no success. Your Majesty, even if out of old favor you do not impose conspicuous execution, how can you entirely fail to demote and disgrace him to answer the empire!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji remonstrated: "Chenghuan was first to urge war. He drained the empire and won nothing in the end. Even if old friendship keeps you from executing him publicly, how can you leave him wholly unpunished and answer to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 給事中段平仲、呂元膺言承璀可斬。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Duan Pingzhong and Lü Yuanying said Chenghuan deserved execution.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officials Duan Pingzhong and Lü Yuanying argued that Chenghuan deserved to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 李絳奏稱：「陛下不責承璀，他日復有敗軍之將，何以處之？

translations.literal: Li Jiang submitted saying: "If Your Majesty does not hold Chenghuan accountable, on another day when there is again a general who loses his army, how will you deal with him?
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang memorialized: "If Chenghuan goes unpunished, what standard will you apply the next time a general leads his army to defeat?

sentences.zh: 若或誅之，則同罪異罰，彼必不服；

translations.literal: If you sometimes execute such a man, then the same crime receives different punishment—they surely will not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Execute the next one and you will have punished the same offense differently—others will not accept that;

sentences.zh: 若或釋之，則誰不保身而玩寇乎！

translations.literal: if you sometimes release such a man, then who will not protect himself and toy with the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: pardon the next one and every commander will think first of self-preservation and treat the enemy lightly!

sentences.zh: 願陛下割不忍之恩，行不易之典，使將帥有所懲勸。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would cut off the kindness you cannot bear and execute the law that is not easy, so that generals and commanders may have both warning and encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: Cut through personal reluctance and enforce the law without exception, so that commanders have both warning and incentive."

sentences.zh: 間二日，上罷承璀中尉，降為軍器使。

translations.literal: Two days later, the emperor removed Chenghuan from the post of Inner Attendant and demoted him to Commissioner of Military Equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the emperor stripped Chenghuan of his post as Inner Attendant and reduced him to Commissioner of Military Equipment.

sentences.zh: 中外相賀。

translations.literal: Within and without the court, all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 裴垍得風疾，上甚惜之，中使候問旁午於道。

translations.literal: Pei Ji contracted wind ailment. The emperor greatly treasured him; palace envoys came in succession along the road to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji fell ill with a paralytic disorder, the emperor was deeply concerned and sent palace envoys in an unbroken stream to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以太常卿權德輿為禮部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Quan Deyu was made Minister of Rites and Associate Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Quan Deyu, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was appointed Minister of Rites and named Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 義武節度使張茂昭請除代人，欲舉族入朝。

translations.literal: Zhang Maozhao, military governor of Yiwu, requested that a successor be appointed and wished to bring his entire clan to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhao, military governor of Yiwu, asked the throne to name his replacement and to allow his whole family to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 河北諸鎮互遣人說止之，茂昭不從，凡四上表。

translations.literal: The various Hebei garrisons each sent men to persuade him to stop; Maozhao did not listen, and in all submitted four memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The other Hebei governors sent envoys one after another urging him to reconsider, but Maozhao refused. He submitted four memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 上乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally granted his request.

sentences.zh: 以左庶子任迪簡為義武行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Left Household Companion Ren Dijian was made campaigning army chief secretary of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Dijian, Left Household Companion, was appointed acting chief secretary of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 茂昭悉以易、定二州簿書管鑰授迪簡，遣其妻子先行，曰：「吾不欲子孫染於污俗。」

translations.literal: Maozhao entirely handed over to Dijian the ledgers, documents, and keys of Yi and Ding prefectures, sent his wife and children ahead, and said: "I do not wish my descendants stained by a corrupt custom."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao turned over all the records and keys of Yi and Ding prefectures to Dijian, sent his family ahead to the capital, and said: "I do not want my descendants tainted by the customs of corrupt rule."

sentences.zh: 茂昭既去，冬，十月，戊寅，虞侯楊伯玉作亂，囚迪簡，辛已，義武將士共殺伯玉。

translations.literal: After Maozhao had departed, in winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Garrison Officer Yang Boyu raised a rebellion, imprisoned Dijian, and on xinsi the officers and soldiers of Yiwu jointly killed Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: After Maozhao had left, in winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the garrison officer Yang Boyu mutinied and seized Ren Dijian. On xinsi the troops of Yiwu rose together and killed Boyu.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使張佐元又作亂，囚迪簡，迪簡乞歸朝。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Zuoyuan again raised a rebellion, imprisoned Dijian, and Dijian begged to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: The army affairs commissioner Zhang Zuoyuan mutinied again, seized Ren Dijian, and Dijian petitioned to be allowed to go to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而將士復殺佐元，奉迪簡主軍務。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the officers and soldiers again killed Zuoyuan and upheld Dijian to preside over military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the troops killed Zuoyuan themselves and restored Dijian to command.

sentences.zh: 時易定府庫罄竭，閭閻亦空，迪簡無以犒士，乃設糲飯與士卒共食之，身居戟門下經月。

translations.literal: At that time the treasuries of Yi and Ding were exhausted, the lanes and wards were empty as well, Dijian had no means to reward the troops, so he prepared coarse rice and ate together with the soldiers, himself dwelling beneath the halberd gate for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Ding's stores were empty and the towns were stripped bare. Unable to reward his men, Dijian served plain rice and ate with the rank and file, sleeping under the barracks gate for an entire month.

sentences.zh: 將士感之，共請迪簡還寢，然後得安其位。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were moved by this, jointly requesting Dijian return to his quarters, and only then was he able to settle in his proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the troops together asked him to move back indoors; only then did he take up his proper station.

sentences.zh: 上命以綾絹十萬匹賜易定將士。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that one hundred thousand bolts of silk be bestowed upon the officers and soldiers of Yi and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a gift of one hundred thousand bolts of silk for the troops of Yi and Ding.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以迪簡為義武節度使。

translations.literal: On renchen, Dijian was made Military Governor of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Ren Dijian was appointed military governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以張茂昭為河中、慈、隰、晉、絳節度使，從行將校皆拜官。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Zhang Maozhao was made Military Governor of Hezhong, Ci, Xi, Jin, and Jiang; the officers who accompanied him on the journey were all granted appointments.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zhang Maozhao was named military governor of Hezhong and the prefectures of Ci, Xi, Jin, and Jiang, and every officer who had come with him received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 右金吾大將軍伊慎以錢三萬緡賂右軍中尉第五從直，求河中節度使。

translations.literal: Right Gold Crow Guard General Yi Shen used thirty thousand strings of cash to bribe Right Army Commandant Diwu Congzhi, seeking the post of Hezhong Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Right Gold Crow Guard General Yi Shen paid thirty thousand strings of cash to bribe Right Army Commandant Diwu Congzhi in hopes of obtaining the Hezhong governorship.

sentences.zh: 從直恐事洩，奏之。

translations.literal: Congzhi feared the matter would leak out and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Congzhi reported the bribe to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚子，貶慎為右衛將軍，坐死者三人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengzi, Shen was demoted to Right Guard General; three persons were put to death in connection with the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengzi, Yi Shen was demoted to Right Guard General, and three others were executed for their part in the scandal.

sentences.zh: 初，慎自安州入朝，留其子宥主留事，朝廷因以為安州刺史，未能去也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shen entered court from Anzhou, he left his son You in charge of remaining affairs; the court accordingly appointed You Anzhou Prefect, and he was unable to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Shen had earlier come to court from Anzhou, he left his son You to manage affairs there; the court then named You prefect of Anzhou, and the son could not quit his post.

sentences.zh: 會宥母卒於長安，宥利於兵權，不時發喪。

translations.literal: When You's mother died in Chang'an, You coveted the military authority and did not promptly send off the funeral procession.
translations.idiomatic: When You's mother died in the capital, he clung to his command and delayed sending the funeral cortege.

sentences.zh: 鄂岳觀察使郗士美遣僚屬以事過其境，宥出迎，因告以凶問，先備籃輿，即日遣之。

translations.literal: E-Yue Observation Commissioner Xi Shimei dispatched a subordinate on business passing through the territory; You came out to meet him, and Shimei informed him of the death notice, prepared a palanquin in advance, and sent him off that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When E-Yue observation commissioner Xi Shimei sent a staff member through the region on business, You came out to greet him. Shimei broke the news of his mother's death, had a litter ready, and dispatched him to the capital that very day.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，會王纁薨。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Prince of Hui Wang Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Prince of Hui Wang Xun passed away.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以前河中節度使王鍔為河東節度使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, former Hezhong Military Governor Wang E was made Hedong Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Wang E, formerly military governor of Hezhong, was transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 上左右受鍔厚賂，多稱譽之，上命鍔兼平章事，李籓固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Those around the emperor received heavy bribes from E and spoke much in his praise; the emperor ordered E also appointed Grand Counselor, but Li Fan firmly held that this was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers around the emperor, having taken lavish gifts from Wang E, showered him with praise. The emperor wished to make him a grand counselor as well, but Li Fan adamantly objected.

sentences.zh: 權德輿曰：「宰相非序進之官。

translations.literal: Quan Deyu said: "The position of Grand Counselor is not an office of sequential advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu said: "Counselor is not a post one advances into by seniority alone.

sentences.zh: 唐興以來，方鎮非大忠大勳，則跋扈者，朝廷或不得已而加之。

translations.literal: Since the founding of Tang, unless a frontier commander possessed great loyalty or great merit, those who were overbearing— the court sometimes added the title only when it had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tang rose, the court has bestowed the title on military governors only when they showed great loyalty or great merit—or when insubordinate men left it no alternative.

sentences.zh: 今鍔既無忠勳，朝廷又非不得已，何為遽以此名假之！」

translations.literal: Now E has neither loyalty nor merit, and the court is not without choice— why should this title be so hastily lent to him!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang E has shown neither loyalty nor achievement, and the court is under no compulsion now. Why rush to confer on him a name he has not earned?"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the emperor dropped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 鍔有吏才，工於完聚。

translations.literal: E had talent for administration and was skilled at replenishing and amassing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E was an able administrator and excelled at rebuilding revenues and stockpiling supplies.

sentences.zh: 范希朝以河東全軍出屯河北，耗散甚眾。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao had taken the entire Hedong army out to encamp in Hebei, dissipating very many.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao had marched the whole Hedong force north to Hebei, draining the region badly.

sentences.zh: 鍔到鎮之初，兵不滿三萬人，馬不過六百匹，歲餘，兵至五萬人，馬有五千匹，器械精利，倉庫充實，又進家財三十萬緡，上復欲加鍔平章事。

translations.literal: When E first arrived at his post, the troops numbered fewer than thirty thousand and horses no more than six hundred; within little more than a year, troops reached fifty thousand and horses five thousand, weapons and equipment were sharp and excellent, storehouses were full, and he further presented three hundred thousand strings of his family wealth— the emperor again wished to add E as Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang E first took command, he had fewer than thirty thousand men and no more than six hundred horses. Within a year he had fifty thousand troops and five thousand mounts, sharp weaponry, and full granaries, and he also presented three hundred thousand strings from his personal fortune. The emperor again proposed making him grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 李絳諫曰：「鍔在太原，雖頗著績效，今因獻家財而命之，若後世何！」

translations.literal: Li Jue remonstrated: "Though E at Taiyuan has achieved considerable results, to appoint him now because he has presented family wealth— what would posterity think!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue warned: "Wang E has indeed done well at Taiyuan, but if you appoint him grand counselor because he paid in family wealth, what precedent will you leave for later ages?"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事裴垍數以疾辭位。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor Pei Ji repeatedly resigned his post on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, vice director of the Secretariat and grand counselor, repeatedly asked to step down, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 庚申，罷為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he was dismissed and made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, he was removed from the chancellorship and appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，張茂昭入朝，請遷祖考之骨於京兆。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Zhang Maozhao entered court and requested that the bones of his ancestors and father be relocated to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Zhang Maozhao came to court and asked permission to move the remains of his forebears to the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以御史中丞呂元膺為鄂岳觀察使。

translations.literal: On renwu, Censor-in-Chief Lü Yuanying was made E-Yue Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Censor-in-Chief Lü Yuanying was appointed observation commissioner of Ezhou and Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 元膺嘗欲夜登城，門已鎖，守者不為開。

translations.literal: Yuanying once wished to ascend the city wall at night; the gate was already locked, and the guard would not open it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuanying once tried to go up on the city wall at night, but the gate was bolted and the sentry refused to let him through.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「中丞也。」

translations.literal: His attendants said: "It is the Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: His escort protested: "This is the censor-in-chief."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「夜中難辯真偽，雖中丞亦不可。」

translations.literal: The guard replied: "In the middle of the night it is hard to distinguish true from false; even if you are the Censor-in-Chief, it is not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: The sentry answered: "At night one cannot tell who is real and who is not. Even if you truly are the censor-in-chief, I still may not open the gate."

sentences.zh: 元膺乃還。

translations.literal: Yuanying then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying turned back.

sentences.zh: 明日，擢為重職。

translations.literal: The next day, he was promoted to an important post.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the sentry was promoted to a senior position.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士、司勳郎中李張面陳吐突承璀專橫，語極懇切。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician and Director of Merit Li Jue faced the emperor and stated that TuTu Chengcui was arbitrary and overbearing; his words were extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician and director in the Ministry of Personnel Li Jue spoke directly to the emperor against TuTu Chengcui's tyrannical conduct, pleading with unusual passion.

sentences.zh: 上作色曰：「卿言太過！」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: "Your words go too far!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened and he said: "You have overstepped yourself!"

sentences.zh: 絳泣曰：「陛下置臣於腹心耳目之地，若臣畏避左右，愛身不言，是臣負陛下；

translations.literal: Jue wept and said: "Your Majesty has placed me where I serve as your heart, eyes, and ears; if I fear those at your side, cherish my own person, and do not speak, then I fail Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue wept and said: "Your Majesty posted me where I am your inner counsel and your eyes and ears. If I shrink from those around you, spare myself, and keep silent, I betray you;

sentences.zh: 言之而陛下惡聞，乃陛下負臣也。」

translations.literal: if I speak and Your Majesty hates to hear it, then Your Majesty fails me."
translations.idiomatic: If I speak honestly and Your Majesty refuses to listen, then it is Your Majesty who fails me."

sentences.zh: 上怒解，曰：「卿所言皆人所不能言，使聯聞所不聞，真忠臣也！

translations.literal: The emperor's anger dissolved, and he said: "What you have said is what others cannot say, and has let Us hear what We had not heard— a true loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: His anger eased, and he said: "You have said what others dare not say and told me what I had never heard. That is the mark of a true loyal subject!

sentences.zh: 他日盡言，皆應如是。」

translations.literal: On other days, speak fully; all should be as today."
translations.idiomatic: Speak plainly to me always, as you have today."

sentences.zh: 己丑，以絳為中書舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: On jichou, Jue was made Secretariat Drafter, retaining his Hanlin post as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Li Jue was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat while keeping his Hanlin appointment.

sentences.zh: 絳嘗從容諫上聚財，上曰：「今兩河數十州，皆國家政令所不及，河、湟數千里，淪於左衽，朕日夜思雪祖宗之恥，而財力不贍，故不得不蓄聚耳。

translations.literal: Jue once calmly remonstrated with the emperor about amassing wealth; the emperor said: "Today dozens of prefectures in the two He regions lie entirely beyond the reach of the state's government orders; for thousands of li along the Yellow River and Huang regions, all has fallen under alien rule. We day and night think of wiping away the shame of our forebears, yet financial strength is insufficient— hence We cannot but store and gather.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue once gently urged the emperor to stop hoarding treasure. The emperor replied: "Scores of prefectures between the Yellow and Huai rivers are beyond my government's reach, and for thousands of miles along the Yellow River and the Huang lands we have lost the heartland to foreign rule. Day and night I burn to avenge the dishonor to our ancestors, yet I lack the means— that is why I must build reserves.

sentences.zh: 不然，朕宮中用度極儉薄，多藏何用邪！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, Our palace expenses are extremely frugal— what use is there in hoarding much!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I live very plainly in the palace. What good would piles of treasure do me?
[End of speech.]"

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝上之下元和六年（

translations.literal: Below the second part of the reign account of Emperor Xianzong Zhao Wen Zhang Wu Da Sheng Zhi Shen Xiao, Yuanhe year 6 (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the annals of Emperor Xianzong, styled Zhao Wen Zhang Wu Da Sheng Zhi Shen Xiao, Yuanhe year 6 (

sentences.zh: 辛卯，公元八一一年）

translations.literal: xinmao, corresponding to the year 811 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinmao [in the sexagenary cycle], equivalent to 811 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲辰，以彰義留後吳少陽為節度使。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiachen, Wu Shaoyang, acting governor of Zhangyi, was made Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiachen, Wu Shaoyang, the interim Zhangyi governor, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以前淮南節度使李吉甫為中書侍郎，同平章事。

translations.literal: On gengshen, former Huainan Military Governor Li Jifu was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Li Jifu, former military governor of Huainan, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 二月壬申，李籓罷為太子詹事。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the second month, Li Fan was dismissed and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the second month, Li Fan was removed from office and named grand mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 己丑，忻王造薨。

translations.literal: On jichou, Prince of Xin Li Zao died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Prince of Xin Li Zao passed away.

sentences.zh: 宦官惡李絳在翰林，以為戶部侍郎，判本司。

translations.literal: The eunuchs hated Li Jiang's presence in the Hanlin Academy and had him made Vice Minister of Revenue, with charge of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Because the eunuchs resented Li Jiang's influence in the Hanlin Academy, they maneuvered to appoint him Vice Minister of Revenue with supervisory charge of that ministry.

sentences.zh: 上問絳：「故事，戶部侍郎皆進羨餘，卿獨無進，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Jiang: "By precedent, vice ministers of revenue all present surplus funds; you alone have presented none—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Li Jiang: "By custom, vice ministers of revenue all submit surplus revenues to the throne. You alone have submitted nothing. Why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「守士之官，厚斂於人以市私恩，天下猶共非之。

translations.literal: He replied: "Officials who guard the land, who heavily levy on the people to trade for private favor—even the empire jointly censures them.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Even when territorial officials levy heavily on the people to buy private goodwill, the whole realm condemns them.

sentences.zh: 況戶部所掌，皆陛下府庫之物，給納有籍，安得羨餘！

translations.literal: How much more so the Ministry of Revenue's charge—all are things in Your Majesty's treasury stores; disbursement and receipt have registers—how could there be surplus!
translations.idiomatic: How much more so here: everything the Ministry of Revenue administers belongs to Your Majesty's treasury, with receipts and disbursements fully recorded. How could there be any surplus to present!

sentences.zh: 若自左藏輸之內藏以為進奉，是猶東庫移之西庫，臣不敢踵此弊也。」

translations.literal: If one transfers from the Left Storehouse to the Inner Storehouse as tribute presentation, it is like moving from the eastern storehouse to the western storehouse—I dare not follow in this abuse."
translations.idiomatic: To shift funds from the Left Treasury to the Inner Treasury and call it tribute would be no more than moving goods from one storehouse to another. I cannot follow such a corrupt practice."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其直，益重之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his straightforwardness and valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his frankness and held him in even higher regard.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，上問宰相：「為政寬猛何先？」

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the emperor asked the chief ministers: "In governing, leniency and severity—which comes first?"
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the emperor asked his chief ministers: "In governing the realm, should leniency or severity come first?"

sentences.zh: 權德輿對曰：「秦以慘刻而亡，漢以寬大而興。

translations.literal: Quan Deyu replied: "Qin perished through cruel harshness; Han rose through generous magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu answered: "Qin fell because its rule was cruel and harsh; Han rose because its rule was generous and broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 太宗觀《明堂圖》，禁杖人背，是故安、史以來，屢有悖逆之臣，皆旋踵自亡，由祖宗仁政結於人心，人不能忘故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong viewed the Hall of Brightness Diagram and forbade flogging people's backs; therefore since An and Shi, though repeatedly there have been rebellious ministers, all have perished in quick succession, because the benevolent government of the ancestral sovereigns is bound in people's hearts and people cannot forget—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong examined the Hall of Brightness diagram, he forbade beating men on the back. That is why, since the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions, though rebellious ministers have arisen time and again, they have all quickly destroyed themselves: the benevolent policies of our forebears are woven into the people's hearts, and those hearts cannot forget.

sentences.zh: 然則寬猛之先後可見矣。」

translations.literal: Thus then the precedence of leniency and severity can be seen."
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear which should come first—leniency or severity."

sentences.zh: 上善其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰，以兵部尚書裴垍為太子賓客，李吉甫惡之也。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day wuchen, the Minister of War Pei Ji was made Guardian of the Heir Apparent—because Li Jifu hated him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on wuchen, Minister of War Pei Ji was appointed Guardian of the Heir Apparent—a demotion engineered by Li Jifu, who had come to despise him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以刑部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使盧坦為戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Vice Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Lu Tan was made Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the Bureau of Public Finance.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Lu Tan, vice minister of justice and salt and iron transport commissioner, was appointed vice minister of revenue with supervisory charge of the Bureau of Public Finance.

sentences.zh: 或告泗州刺史薛謇為代北水運使，有異馬不以獻。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Sizhou Prefect Xue Shen, while serving as transport commissioner for northern routes by water, had a fine horse but did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone denounced Xue Shen, prefect of Sizhou, for withholding a fine horse while serving as northern-route transport commissioner by water.

sentences.zh: 事下度支，使巡官往驗，未返，上遲之，使品官劉泰昕按其事。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Bureau of Public Finance, which dispatched an inspector to verify; before he returned, the emperor grew impatient and sent ranking official Liu Taixin to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Bureau of Public Finance, which sent an inspector to verify it. Before the inspector returned, the emperor grew impatient and dispatched Liu Taixin, a ranking court official, to investigate on his own.

sentences.zh: 戶坦曰：「陛下既使有司驗之，又使品官繼往，豈大臣不足信於品官乎！

translations.literal: Lu Tan said: "Your Majesty, having already had the responsible offices verify it, again sends a ranking official to follow after—is a great minister not worthy of trust compared with a ranking official!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan protested: "Your Majesty has already ordered the proper offices to investigate, yet now sends another ranking official after them. Does this mean that a senior minister is less trustworthy than a low-ranked court officer?

sentences.zh: 臣請先就黜免。」

translations.literal: Your subject requests first to accept dismissal and removal."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that I be dismissed at once."

sentences.zh: 上召泰昕還。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Taixin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Liu Taixin.

sentences.zh: 五月，前行營糧料使於皋謨、董溪坐贓數千緡，敕貸其死，皋謨流春州，溪流封州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, former Forward Camp Provision Commissioner Yu Gaomo and Dong Xi were guilty of embezzlement of several thousand strings of cash; an edict spared their death; Gaomo was banished to Chunzhou, Xi to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Yu Gaomo and Dong Xi, former commissioners of provisions for the forward camp, were convicted of embezzling several thousand strings of cash. An edict commuted their death sentences: Gaomo was exiled to Chunzhou and Xi to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至潭州，並追遣中使賜死。

translations.literal: When they reached Tanzhou, both were pursued and eunuch envoys were dispatched to grant death.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Tanzhou, the emperor sent eunuch messengers after them and had both put to death.

sentences.zh: 權德輿上言，以為：「皋謨等罪當死，陛下肆諸市朝，誰不懼法！

translations.literal: Quan Deyu submitted a memorial, saying: "Gaomo and the others deserved death; had Your Majesty displayed them in the marketplace and court, who would not fear the law!
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu memorialized the throne, arguing: "Yu Gaomo and his associates deserved to die. Had Your Majesty executed them publicly, who would not have trembled before the law!

sentences.zh: 不當已赦而殺之。」

translations.literal: One should not, having already pardoned them, then kill them."
translations.idiomatic: They should not have been killed after a pardon had already been granted."

sentences.zh: 溪，晉之子也。

translations.literal: Xi was Jin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi was the son of Dong Jin.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以金吾大將軍李惟簡為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Right Gold Guard General Li Weijian was made military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Right Gold Guard General Li Weijian was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 隴州地與吐蕃接，舊常朝夕相伺，更入攻抄，人不得息。

translations.literal: Longzhou's territory borders on Tibet; formerly morning and evening they watched each other, alternately entering to raid and plunder, and the people could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou bordered Tibetan territory, where the frontier garrisons had long watched each other from dawn to dusk, raiding back and forth until the people knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 惟簡以為邊將當謹守備，蓄財谷以待寇，不當睹小利，起事盜恩，禁不得妄入其地。

translations.literal: Weijian considered that frontier generals ought carefully to guard defenses, store grain and provisions to await invaders, and ought not to eye small gains, stir up incidents to steal imperial favor; he forbade unauthorized entry into the other's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian held that frontier commanders should maintain strong defenses, stockpile grain, and wait for any invasion—not seize on petty skirmishes to claim credit and imperial favor. He forbade unauthorized incursions into enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 益市耕牛，鑄農器，以給農之不能自具者，增墾田數十萬畝。

translations.literal: He further purchased plow oxen and cast farm implements to supply farmers who could not provide for themselves, increasing reclaimed fields by several hundred thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: He bought more plowing oxen and had farm tools cast for peasants who could not afford their own, opening several hundred thousand mu of new farmland.

sentences.zh: 屬歲屢稔，公私有餘，販者流及它方。

translations.literal: As the years were repeatedly abundant, public and private stores had surplus, and traders flowed to other regions.
translations.idiomatic: With several successive good harvests, both public and private granaries overflowed, and surplus grain flowed to other regions through trade.

sentences.zh: 賜振武節度使阿跌光進姓李氏。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of Zhenwu, Atai Guangjin, was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Atai Guangjin, military commissioner of Zhenwu, was granted the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯，李吉甫奏：「自漢至隋十有三代，設官之多，無如國家者。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingmao, Li Jifu memorialized: "From Han through Sui there were thirteen dynasties; in the multitude of offices established, none matches our state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingmao, Li Jifu submitted a memorial: "From Han through Sui, thirteen dynasties have ruled China. In the sheer number of offices they established, none compares with our own.

sentences.zh: 天寶以後，中原宿兵，見在可計者八十餘萬，其餘為商賈、僧、道不服田畝者什有五六，是常以三分勞筋苦骨之人奉七分待衣坐食之輩也。

translations.literal: After Tianbao, in the Central Plains garrison troops, those presently countable numbered more than eight hundred thousand; the rest—merchants, monks, and Daoists who do not submit to field assessment—are five or six in ten; thus ordinarily three parts of those who labor sinew and bone support seven parts of those who wait for clothes and sit and eat.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tianbao era, garrison forces in the Central Plains alone number more than eight hundred thousand on the rolls, while merchants, monks, and Daoists exempt from field taxation make up five or six tenths of the rest of the population. Thus three parts of those who toil with bone and sinew support seven parts who simply await their clothing and live at ease.

sentences.zh: 今內外官以稅錢給俸者不下萬員，天下千三百餘縣，或以一縣之地而為州，一鄉之民而為縣者甚眾，請敕有司詳定廢置，吏員可省者省之，州縣可並者並之，入仕之塗可減者減之。

translations.literal: Now internal and external officials paid salaries from tax funds number no less than ten thousand; throughout the empire there are more than thirteen hundred counties, but very many places where one county's territory becomes a prefecture, one township's people become a county—request that an edict order the responsible offices to examine in detail abolitions and establishments; officials who can be reduced, reduce them; prefectures and counties that can be merged, merge them; paths of entering office that can be reduced, reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand civil officials inside and outside the capital now draw salaries from tax revenues. Though the empire has more than thirteen hundred counties, many are prefectures no larger than a single county, or counties no larger than a single township. I ask that Your Majesty order the responsible offices to review what should be abolished or retained: cut redundant posts wherever possible, merge prefectures and counties where feasible, and reduce the avenues by which men enter office.

sentences.zh: 又，國家舊章，依品制俸，官一品月俸錢三十緡；

translations.literal: Further, the state's old statutes, according to rank setting salaries—a first-rank official's monthly salary cash thirty strings;
translations.idiomatic: Further, under the dynasty's original regulations, salaries were set by rank: a first-rank official received thirty strings of cash per month;

sentences.zh: 職田祿米不過千斛。

translations.literal: Official fields and salary grain did not exceed one thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: stipends from official fields and grain allowances did not exceed one thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 艱難以來，增置使額，厚給俸錢，大歷中，權臣月俸至九千緡，州無大小，刺史皆千緡。

translations.literal: Since the times of hardship, additional commissioner posts were established and salaries generously granted; in the Dali era, powerful ministers' monthly salaries reached nine thousand strings; prefectures regardless of size, prefects all received one thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Since the troubled years, new commissioner posts have proliferated and salaries have swollen. By the Dali era, powerful ministers drew monthly salaries of up to nine thousand strings, and every prefect—regardless of the prefecture's size—received one thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 常兗為相。

translations.literal: Chang Yan served as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Yan became chief minister,

sentences.zh: 始立限約，李泌又量其閒劇，隨事增加，時謂通濟，理難減削。

translations.literal: He first established limits and terms; Li Bi again measured their leisure and urgency, increasing according to circumstances; at the time it was called practical relief, and in principle difficult to reduce and cut.
translations.idiomatic: he first set limits on official salaries. Li Bi later adjusted them according to the light or heavy burden of each post, adding compensation where needed. At the time this was praised as a workable remedy, and in principle it has been hard to scale back.

sentences.zh: 然猶有名存職廢，或額去俸存，閒劇之間，厚薄頓異。

translations.literal: Yet still there are cases where the name remains but the duty is abolished, or the quota removed but salary remains; between leisure and urgency, thick and thin suddenly differ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet offices often survive in name after their functions have lapsed, or salaries continue after posts have been abolished. Between easy and demanding assignments, compensation varies sharply and unevenly.

sentences.zh: 請敕有司詳考俸料、雜給，量定以聞。」

translations.literal: Request that an edict order the responsible offices to examine in detail salary provisions and miscellaneous grants, measure and fix them, and report."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order the responsible offices to review all salary provisions and supplementary allowances in detail, fix appropriate amounts, and report back."

sentences.zh: 於是命給事中段平仲、中書舍人韋貫之、兵部侍郎許孟容、戶部侍郎李絳同詳定。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Supervising Secretary Duan Pingzhong, Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat Wei Guanzhi, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jiang jointly to examine and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Supervising Secretary Duan Pingzhong, Secretariat drafting secretary Wei Guanzhi, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jiang to review the matter together.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，富平人梁悅報父仇，殺秦杲，自詣縣請罪。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, Liang Yue of Fuping avenged his father's death, killed Qin Gao, and went on his own to the county to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the ninth month, Liang Yue of Fuping avenged his father by killing Qin Gao, then went to the county magistrate of his own accord to surrender.

sentences.zh: 敕：「復仇，據《禮經》則義不同天，征法令則殺人者死。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Blood vengeance—according to the Book of Rites, the duty is as weighty as heaven itself; measured against the statutes, one who kills shall die.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Blood vengeance: by the Book of Rites, the duty is as sacred as heaven itself; by the statutes, a killer must die.

sentences.zh: 禮、法二事，皆王教之大端，有此異同，固資論辯，宜令都省集議聞奏。」

translations.literal: Rites and law are both great foundations of royal instruction; with this difference and sameness, debate is naturally called for—order the Department of State Affairs to assemble for joint deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: Rites and law are both pillars of royal instruction. Where they conflict, debate is warranted. Let the Department of State Affairs convene for joint deliberation and report its findings."

sentences.zh: 職方員外郎韓愈議，以為：「律無其條，非闕文也。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments Han Yu submitted an opinion, saying: "The code has no provision for this—not because the text is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, vice director in the Bureau of Appointments, argued: "The law contains no provision on this point—not because the text is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 蓋以不許復仇，則傷孝子之心而乖先王之訓；

translations.literal: It is because if one does not permit blood vengeance, one wounds the heart of the filial son and departs from the instruction of the former kings;
translations.idiomatic: For if blood vengeance were forbidden outright, it would wound the heart of the filial son and betray the teaching of the ancient kings;

sentences.zh: 許復仇，則人將倚法專殺，無以禁止其端矣。

translations.literal: if one permits blood vengeance, then people will rely on the law to kill on their own authority, and there will be no way to restrain the beginning of it.
translations.idiomatic: yet if blood vengeance were permitted freely, men would invoke the law to kill at will, and there would be no way to check the abuse at its source.

sentences.zh: 故聖人丁寧其義於經，而深沒其文於律，其意將使法吏一斷於法，而經術之士得引經而議也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage repeatedly admonished its meaning in the classics, yet deeply buried its text in the code; his intent was to have legal officers decide solely by the law, while scholars of the classics might cite the classics in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sages emphasized the principle in the classics yet deliberately omitted explicit language from the statutes: legal officers were to decide cases by law alone, while scholars of the classics might invoke the classics in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 宜定其制曰：『凡復父仇者，事發，具申尚書省集議奏聞，酌其宜而處之。』

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the regulation thus: 'All who avenge a father's death, when the matter arises, shall fully report to the Department of State Affairs for joint deliberation and memorial to the throne, and the appropriate disposition shall be weighed and applied.'
translations.idiomatic: The proper regulation would read: 'Whenever anyone avenges a father's death, upon the matter coming to light, the case shall be reported in full to the Department of State Affairs for joint deliberation and memorial to the throne, and an appropriate disposition shall be determined.'

sentences.zh: 則經律無失其指矣。」

translations.literal: Then the classics and the code would not lose their intent."
translations.idiomatic: In this way neither the classics nor the statutes would lose their proper meaning."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，敕：「梁悅杖一百，流循州。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, an edict stated: "Liang Yue shall receive one hundred blows with the staff and be banished to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, an edict ordered: "Liang Yue shall be flogged one hundred strokes and exiled to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，吏部奏准敕並省內外官計八百八員，諸司流外一千七百六十九人。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, the Ministry of Personnel memorialized that, pursuant to an edict, internal and external offices were consolidated and reduced by a total of eight hundred eight posts, and extrabureau personnel in the various offices by one thousand seven hundred sixty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Ministry of Personnel reported that, under imperial decree, a total of 808 posts in offices at court and in the provinces had been consolidated, along with 1,769 extrabureau personnel in the various departments.

sentences.zh: 黔州大水壞城郭，觀察使竇群發溪洞蠻以治之。

translations.literal: A great flood at Qian Prefecture destroyed the walls and outworks; Observation Commissioner Dou Qun mobilized the tribesmen of the stream valleys and cave settlements to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: Catastrophic flooding at Qianzhou breached the city walls. Observation Commissioner Dou Qun conscripted tribal peoples from the hill streams and cave settlements to make repairs.

sentences.zh: 督役太急，於是辰、漵二州蠻反，群討之，不能定。

translations.literal: The supervision of the labor was too hurried; thereupon the tribes of Chen and Xu Prefectures rebelled. Qun attacked them but could not suppress the disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The corvée was driven too hard. The tribes of Chen and Xu prefectures rose in revolt. Dou Qun marched against them but could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 戊午，貶群開州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Qun was demoted to governor of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Dou Qun was demoted to governor of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，弓箭庫使劉希光受羽林大將軍孫瑞錢二萬緡，為求方鎮，事覺，賜死。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Liu Xiguang, commissioner of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, received twenty thousand strings of cash from Sun Rui, grand general of the Feathered Forest Army, to procure a military governorship for him; when the matter came to light, he was sentenced to death by imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Liu Xiguang, keeper of the bow and arrow arsenal, accepted twenty thousand strings of cash from Sun Rui, a general of the Imperial Guard, to secure him a post as military governor. When the bribery was exposed, the emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 事連左衛上將軍、知內待省事吐突承璀，丙申，以承璀為淮南監軍。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Tutu Chenghuan, left guard senior general and director of palace domestic affairs; on the day bingshen, Chenghuan was appointed military supervisor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The case also implicated Tutu Chenghuan, senior general of the Left Guard and director of the Palace Domestic Service Bureau. On bingshen, Chenghuan was sent out as military supervisor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 上問李絳：「聯出承璀何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Li Jiang: "What do you think of my sending Chenghuan away?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Li Jiang, "What do you think of my dispatching Chenghuan?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「外人不意陛下遽能如是。」

translations.literal: Li Jiang replied: "Outsiders did not expect Your Majesty suddenly to be capable of acting thus."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang answered, "Your subjects hardly expected that Your Majesty would act so decisively, and so soon."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此家奴耳，向以其驅使之久，故假以恩私；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He is merely a household slave. Before, because I had long put him to service, I granted him private favor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is nothing but a household slave. I indulged him with private favor only because I had commanded his service for so long;

sentences.zh: 若有違犯，朕去之輕如一毛耳！」

translations.literal: if he violates the law, I would dismiss him as lightly as a single hair!"
translations.idiomatic: but if he breaks the law, I shall cast him off as lightly as a single hair!"

sentences.zh: 十六宅諸王既不出閣，其女嫁不以時，選尚者皆由宦官，率以厚賂自達。

translations.literal: Since the princes of the Sixteen Residences no longer left their quarters, their daughters were not married at the proper season; those selected as consorts for princesses were all chosen by eunuchs, who as a rule gained access through lavish bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Because the princes of the Sixteen Residences no longer left the palace precincts, their daughters went unmarried past the proper age. Matchmaking for imperial consorts passed entirely through eunuchs, who typically secured appointments by offering lavish bribes.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫上言：「自古尚主必擇其人，獨近世不然。」

translations.literal: Li Jifu submitted a memorial: "From antiquity, when bestowing a princess in marriage one always chose the man; only in recent times has this not been so."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu memorialized the throne: "In antiquity, a princess's hand was always given to a man chosen for his worth. Only in recent times has this ceased to be so."

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，詔封恩王等六女為縣主，委中書、門下、宗正、吏部選門地人才稱可者嫁之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renshen, an edict enfeoffed six daughters, including those of Prince En, as district princesses, and charged the Chancellery, the Secretariat, the Court of the Imperial Clan, and the Ministry of Personnel to select men of good lineage and talent deemed suitable and marry them to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, an edict ennobled six daughters of princes, including Prince En, as district princesses and entrusted the Chancellery, Secretariat, Court of the Imperial Clan, and Ministry of Personnel with selecting men of worthy family and proven talent to marry them.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以戶部侍郎李絳為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Li Jiang, vice minister of revenue, was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and concurrent chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Li Jiang, vice minister of revenue, was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫為相，多修舊怨，上頗知之，故擢絳為相。

translations.literal: Li Jifu, as chief minister, pursued many old grievances; the emperor knew this quite well, and therefore elevated Jiang to the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Li Jifu had settled many old scores. The emperor was well aware of this, and promoted Li Jiang to the chancellorship in counterbalance.

sentences.zh: 吉甫善逢迎上意，而絳鯁直，數爭論於上前；

translations.literal: Jifu was skilled at accommodating the emperor's wishes, whereas Jiang was upright and unyielding, and often disputed before the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Jifu excelled at flattering the emperor's wishes, while Jiang was blunt and incorruptible, and often argued with him before the throne;

sentences.zh: 上多直絳而從其言，由是二人有隙。

translations.literal: the emperor mostly sided with Jiang and followed his counsel; thereby the two men came to estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor usually sided with Jiang and took his advice. From this a rift opened between the two men.

sentences.zh: 閏月，辛卯朔，黔州奏：辰、漵賊帥張伯靖寇播州、費州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day of the cycle xinmao, Qian Prefecture reported: the bandit chieftain Zhang Bojing of Chen and Xu raided Bozhou and Feizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the first day xinmao, Qianzhou reported that the rebel leader Zhang Bojing of Chen and Xu had raided Bozhou and Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 試太子通事舍人李涉知上於吐突承璀恩顧未衰，乃投匭上疏，稱「承璀有功，希光無罪。

translations.literal: Li She, probationary palace attendant for the crown prince, knowing that the emperor's favor toward Tutu Chenghuan had not yet waned, submitted a petition through the suggestion box, stating: "Chenghuan had merit; Xiguang was guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Li She, a probationary palace attendant to the crown prince, knowing the emperor's affection for Tutu Chenghuan had not yet cooled, dropped a petition into the suggestion box claiming that "Chenghuan had rendered service, and Xiguang was innocent.

sentences.zh: 承璀久委心腹，不宜遽棄。」

translations.literal: Chenghuan has long been entrusted as a close confidant; he should not be cast aside so abruptly."
translations.idiomatic: Chenghuan has served long as a trusted confidant and ought not to be cast aside so hastily."

sentences.zh: 知匭使、諫議大夫孔癸戈見其副章，詰責不受。

translations.literal: Kong Guige, remonstrance and censure official and commissioner of the suggestion box, saw the duplicate copy, rebuked him, and refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Guige, remonstrance official and keeper of the suggestion box, read the duplicate draft, rebuked Li She, and refused the petition.

sentences.zh: 涉乃行賂，詣光順門通之。

translations.literal: She then offered a bribe and had it passed in through Guangshun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li She then offered a bribe and had the petition smuggled in through Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 癸戈聞之，上疏極言「涉奸險欺天，請加顯戮。」

translations.literal: Guige heard of this and submitted a memorial strongly stating: "She is treacherous, wicked, and deceives Heaven; I ask that he be punished by conspicuous execution."
translations.idiomatic: When Guige learned of this, he memorialized the throne in the strongest terms that "Li She is deceitful, wicked, and mocks Heaven itself, and I beg that he be punished by a public execution."

sentences.zh: 戊申，貶涉峽州司倉。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, She was demoted to warehouse officer of Xiachou.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Li She was demoted to warehouse officer of Xiachou.

sentences.zh: 涉，渤之兄；

translations.literal: She was the elder brother of Bo;
translations.idiomatic: Li She was the elder brother of Li Bo;

sentences.zh: 癸戈，巢父之子也。

translations.literal: Guige was the son of Chaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Guige was the son of Kong Chaofu.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，惠昭太子寧薨。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Crown Prince Hui Zhao Ning died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Crown Prince Ning, posthumously styled Hui Zhao, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下大稔，米斗有直二錢者。

translations.literal: That year the empire enjoyed a great harvest; in some places a dou of rice sold for as little as two cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empire enjoyed an abundant harvest; in places a peck of rice sold for as little as two cash.

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝上之下元和七年（

translations.literal: Below the second part of the reign account of Emperor Xianzong Zhao Wen Zhang Wu Da Sheng Zhi Shen Xiao, Yuanhe year 7 (
translations.idiomatic: Below the second part of the reign account of Emperor Xianzong, the Luminous, Literary, Martial, Greatly Sagacious, Utmost Divine, and Filial — Yuanhe 7 (

sentences.zh: 壬辰，公元八一二年）

translations.literal: renchen, corresponding to the year 812 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renchen, 812 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，以京兆尹元義方為鄜坊觀察使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinwei, Yuan Yifang, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was appointed observation commissioner of Fu and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on xinwei, Yuan Yifang, metropolitan governor of the capital district, was appointed observation commissioner of Fu and Fang.

sentences.zh: 初，義方媚事吐突承璀，李吉甫欲自托於承璀，擢義方為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yifang had curried favor with Tutu Chenghuan; Li Jifu, wishing to attach himself to Chenghuan, promoted Yifang to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Yifang had flattered Tutu Chenghuan. Li Jifu, seeking Chenghuan's patronage, had appointed him metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 李絳惡義方為人，故出之。

translations.literal: Li Jiang disliked Yifang's character and therefore sent him out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang despised Yuan Yifang's character and so had him sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 義方入謝，因言「李絳私其同年許季同，除京兆少尹，出臣鄜坊，專作威福，欺罔聰明。」

translations.literal: Yifang entered to give thanks and thereupon said: "Li Jiang shows favoritism toward his examination-year companion Xu Jitong, appointing him vice metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and sending me out to Fu and Fang — he monopolizes power and profit and deceives Your Majesty's clear vision."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yifang came to thank the emperor, he said, "Li Jiang has shown favor to his examination-year companion Xu Jitong, appointing him vice metropolitan governor while sending me off to Fu and Fang. He wields power for private gain and deceives Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕諳李絳不知是。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am well acquainted with Li Jiang and do not believe this is so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know Li Jiang well and do not believe this.

sentences.zh: 明日，將問之。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow I shall question him."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I shall ask him about it."

sentences.zh: 義方惶愧而出。

translations.literal: Yifang departed in fear and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yifang withdrew, ashamed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 明日，上以詰絳曰：「人於同年固有情乎？」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor questioned Jiang, saying: "Do people naturally feel affection toward their examination-year companions?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor questioned Li Jiang: "Is there naturally special feeling between men who passed the examinations in the same year?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「同年，乃四海九州之人偶同科第，或登科然後相識，情於何有！

translations.literal: Jiang replied: "Examination-year companions are people from the four seas and nine provinces who happen to pass in the same year; some do not even know each other until after passing — what room is there for special feeling!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang replied, "Examination-year companions are simply people from across the empire who happened to pass in the same year. Some never even meet until after the examinations. What special bond could there be!

sentences.zh: 且陛下不以臣愚，備位宰相，宰相職在量才授任，若其人果才，雖在兄弟子侄之中猶將用之，況同年乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, though Your Majesty did not regard me as foolish and installed me in the post of chief minister, a chief minister's duty lies in measuring talent and appointing the worthy; if a man truly possesses talent, I would use him even among brothers, sons, and nephews — how much more so among examination-year companions!
translations.idiomatic: And though Your Majesty has not judged me unfit and has placed me in the chancellorship, a chief minister's duty is to measure talent and assign offices accordingly. If a man is truly capable, I would appoint him even were he my own brother, son, or nephew — to say nothing of an examination-year companion!

sentences.zh: 避嫌而棄才，是乃便身，非徇公也。」

translations.literal: To avoid suspicion and discard talent — that would merely serve oneself, not pursue the public good."
translations.idiomatic: To avoid suspicion by rejecting the capable would serve my private convenience, not the public good."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善，朕知卿必不爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Well said. I know you surely would not act thus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said. I know you would never do such a thing."

sentences.zh: 遂趣義方之官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hurried Yifang to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Yuan Yifang on his way to his new post.

sentences.zh: 振武河溢，毀東受降城。

translations.literal: The Zhenwu River overflowed and destroyed the Eastern Surrender City.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenwu River burst its banks and destroyed the Eastern Surrender City.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌，上御延英殿，李吉甫言：「天下已太平，陛下宜為樂。」

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingxu, the emperor held court in the Yanying Hall. Li Jifu said: "The empire is already at peace; Your Majesty ought to enjoy himself."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingxu, the emperor held court in the Yanying Hall. Li Jifu said, "The empire is now at peace. Your Majesty ought to enjoy himself."

sentences.zh: 李絳曰：「漢文帝時兵木無刃，家給人足，賈誼猶以為厝火積薪之下，不可謂安。

translations.literal: Li Jiang said: "In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, weapons and trees had no edge, and every household was well supplied; yet Jia Yi still took it to be like fire laid beneath piled kindling — it could not be called secure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said, "Under Emperor Wen of Han, weapons grew dull and trees went untrimmed, every household was provided for — yet Jia Yi still likened the realm to firewood stacked over a hidden flame. It could hardly be called secure.

sentences.zh: 今法令所不能制者，河南、北五十餘州。

translations.literal: Today, more than fifty prefectures south and north of the Yellow River lie beyond what the statutes can control.
translations.idiomatic: Today more than fifty prefectures south and north of the Yellow River lie beyond the reach of law and command.

sentences.zh: 犬戎腥膻，近接涇、隴，烽火屢驚。

translations.literal: The Rong tribes reek of rank meat; they press close upon Jing and Long, and beacon fires are repeatedly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The western tribesmen, reeking of mutton and butter, press close upon Jing and Long, and the beacon fires flare again and again.

sentences.zh: 加之水旱時作，倉稟空虛，此正陛下宵衣旰食之時，豈得謂之太平，遽為樂哉！」

translations.literal: Added to this, floods and droughts occur from time to time, and the granaries stand empty; this is precisely the time when Your Majesty should rise before dawn and eat after dark — how can one call it peace and hasten to enjoy oneself!
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought strike again and again, and the storehouses stand empty. This is precisely the hour when Your Majesty should rise before dawn and retire after dark to govern — how can the realm be called at peace, or leisure be urged upon you!

sentences.zh: 上欣然曰：「卿言正合朕意。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "Your words exactly match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, pleased, "Your words are exactly what I mean."

sentences.zh: 退，謂左右曰：「吉甫專為悅媚，如李絳，真宰相也！」

translations.literal: After withdrawing, he said to those around him: "Jifu specializes in pleasing and flattery; someone like Li Jiang—he is a true chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: When he had withdrawn, he said to those around him, "Jifu does nothing but curry favor and flatter. A man like Li Jiang—that is a true chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 上嘗問宰相：「貞元中政事下理，何乃至此？」
