translations.literal: The emperor once asked the chancellors: "During the Zhenyuan era government affairs were poorly managed—how did things reach this point?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor asked the chancellors, "Under the Zhenyuan reign, affairs of state fell into disorder. How did things come to such a pass?"

sentences.zh: 李吉甫對曰：「德宗自任聖智，不信宰相而信他人，是使奸臣得乘間弄威福。

translations.literal: Li Jifu replied: "Emperor Dezong trusted his own sagacity and wisdom, did not trust the chancellors but trusted others—this enabled treacherous ministers to seize openings and manipulate authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu answered, "Emperor Dezong relied on his own wisdom, trusting others rather than his chancellors. That gave treacherous ministers the chance to exploit gaps in power and bend authority to their will.

sentences.zh: 政事不理，職此故也。」

translations.literal: Government affairs were not properly handled—for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: That is why state affairs went unmanaged."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然此亦未必皆德宗之過。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "However, this is not necessarily all Emperor Dezong's fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But this is not necessarily all Dezong's fault.

sentences.zh: 朕幼在德宗左右，見事有得失，當時宰相亦未有再三執奏者，皆懷祿偷安，今日豈得專歸咎於德宗邪！

translations.literal: I was young at Emperor Dezong's side and saw when things had gains and losses. The chancellors of that time also did not repeatedly remonstrate and submit memorials—all clung to their salaries and sought ease. How can one today blame Dezong alone!
translations.idiomatic: When I was young I was at Dezong's side and saw where things succeeded and failed. Even then, not one of the chancellors pressed his objections again and again—they all clung to their stipends and sought comfort. How can we lay all the blame on Dezong today?

sentences.zh: 卿輩宜用此為戒，事有非是，當力陳不已，勿畏朕譴怒而遽止也。」

translations.literal: You should take this as a warning: when affairs are wrong, you should vigorously state your views without stopping; do not fear my rebuke and anger and then quickly cease."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be your warning. When something is wrong, press your case without letup. Do not fear my anger and fall silent at once."

sentences.zh: 李吉甫嘗言：「人臣不當強諫，使君悅臣安，不亦美乎！」

translations.literal: Li Jifu once said: "A subject should not remonstrate forcefully—if the ruler is pleased and the subject is secure, is that not beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu once said, "Ministers ought not to remonstrate too forcefully. If the ruler is content and the minister is secure, is that not a fine thing?"

sentences.zh: 李絳曰：「人臣當犯顏苦口，指陳得失，若陷君於惡，豈得為忠！」

translations.literal: Li Jiang said: "A subject should violate the face and speak bitterly, pointing out gains and losses. If one leads the ruler into evil, how can that be loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said, "A minister ought to risk his sovereign's displeasure and speak bluntly, laying out what is right and wrong. If one steers the ruler toward wrongdoing, how is that loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「絳言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jiang's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Jiang is right."

sentences.zh: 吉甫至中書，臥不視事，長吁而已。

translations.literal: Jifu arrived at the Secretariat, lay down and did not attend to business, sighing deeply—nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu went to the Secretariat, lay down, and refused to conduct business, sighing to himself and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 李絳或久不諫，上輒詰之曰：「豈朕不能容受邪，將無事可諫也？」

translations.literal: When Li Jiang went long without remonstrating, the emperor would press him, saying, "Is it that I cannot bear to accept counsel, or that there is nothing worth remonstrating about?"
translations.idiomatic: If Li Jiang went too long without offering counsel, the emperor would press him: "Do you think I cannot bear remonstrance, or is there simply nothing left to remonstrate about?"

sentences.zh: 李吉甫又嘗言於上曰：「賞罰，人主之二柄，不可偏廢。

translations.literal: Li Jifu also once said to the emperor: "Reward and punishment are the two handles of the ruler—they cannot be abandoned on one side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu again told the emperor, "Reward and punishment are the sovereign's two instruments of rule. Neither can be neglected.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐祚以來，惠澤深矣，而威刑未振，中外懈惰，願加嚴以振之。」

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, gracious benefits have been deep, yet stern punishments have not been invigorated; inside and outside are slack and indolent—I wish you would add severity to invigorate them."
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, your grace has been deep, yet punitive authority has not been sharpened. Court and provinces alike have grown slack. I urge you to tighten discipline and revive awe."

sentences.zh: 上顧李絳曰：「何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Li Jiang and said: "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Li Jiang and asked, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王者之政，尚德不尚刑，豈可捨成、康、文、景而效秦始皇父子乎！」

translations.literal: He replied: "The government of a true king values virtue and does not value punishment—how can one abandon the models of Cheng, Kang, Wen, and Jing to imitate Qin Shihuang and his son!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A true king's rule esteems virtue, not punishment. How can we abandon the examples of Kings Cheng and Kang, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing to imitate Qin Shihuang and his son?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Quite so."

sentences.zh: 後旬餘，-{于}-頔入對，亦勸上峻刑。

translations.literal: More than ten days later, Yu Di came for an audience and also urged the emperor to enforce severe punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than ten days later, Yu Di came to court and likewise urged the emperor to adopt harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 又數日，上謂宰相曰：「-{于}-頔大是奸臣，勸朕峻刑，卿知其意乎？」

translations.literal: A few days later, the emperor said to the chancellors: "Yu Di is very much a treacherous minister—he urged me to enforce severe punishments. Do you know his intent?"
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor told the chancellors, "Yu Di is nothing but a treacherous minister. He urged me to adopt harsh punishments. Do you understand what he was after?"

sentences.zh: 皆對曰：「不知也。」

translations.literal: They all replied: "We do not know."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "We do not."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此欲使朕失人心耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is because he wants to make me lose popular hearts—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He wants to make me lose the people's hearts, that is all."

sentences.zh: 吉甫失色，退而抑首不言笑竟日。

translations.literal: Jifu lost color; after withdrawing he bowed his head and neither spoke nor laughed for the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu turned pale. After he withdrew he kept his head down and spoke and laughed not at all for the rest of the day.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，以庫部郎中、翰林學士崔群為中書舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day bingchen, Ku Department Bureau Chief and Hanlin Academician Cui Qun was appointed Secretariat Reviser, retaining his status as academician.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on bingchen, Cui Qun—bureau chief in the Ku Department and a Hanlin academician—was appointed Secretariat Reviser while retaining his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 上嘉群讜直，命學士「自今奏事，必取崔群連署，然後進之。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised Qun's forthright integrity and ordered the academicians: "From now on when submitting memorials, you must obtain Cui Qun's joint signature before forwarding them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired Qun's frank integrity and ordered the Hanlin academicians, "From now on no memorial may be submitted until Cui Qun has countersigned it."

sentences.zh: 群曰：「翰林舉動皆為故事。

translations.literal: Qun said: "All the actions of the Hanlin follow established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "Everything the Hanlin does follows established precedent.

sentences.zh: 必如是，後來萬一有阿媚之人為之長，則下位直言無從而進矣。」

translations.literal: If it must be so, then if by chance in the future a flatterer becomes its head, those below will have no way to advance straight speech."
translations.idiomatic: If we make this mandatory, then should some flatterer ever head the academy, those beneath him will have no path by which frank counsel can reach the throne."

sentences.zh: 固不奉詔。

translations.literal: He steadfastly did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 章三上，上乃從之。

translations.literal: After three memorials he submitted, the emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted memorials three times, the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚申，上謂宰相曰：「卿輩屢言淮、浙去歲水旱，近有御史自彼還，言不至為災，事竟如何？」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day gengshen, the emperor said to the chancellors: "You have repeatedly said that Huai and Zhe suffered flood and drought last year. Recently a censor returned from there and said it did not amount to disaster. How do matters actually stand?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengshen, the emperor asked the chancellors, "You have repeatedly reported floods and drought in the Huai and Zhe regions last year. A censor recently returned from there and said the damage was not severe. What is the truth?"

sentences.zh: 李絳對曰：「臣按淮南、浙西、浙東奏狀，皆雲水旱，人多流亡，求設法招撫，其意似恐朝廷罪之者，豈肯無災而妄言有災邪！

translations.literal: Li Jiang replied: "Your subject has examined the memorial reports from Huainan, Zhexixi, and Zhedong—all report flood and drought, many people fled and went into exile, and they request measures to recruit and comfort them. Their intent seems to fear the court will blame them—how could they falsely claim disaster when there was none!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang answered, "I have reviewed the reports from Huainan, western Zhe, and eastern Zhe. All describe flood and drought; many people have fled their homes and beg for relief measures. They seem afraid the court will punish them. Why would they invent a disaster where none existed?

sentences.zh: 此蓋御史欲為奸諛以悅上意耳，願得其主名，按致其法。」

translations.literal: This must be the censor seeking to flatter treacherously to please the emperor's mind—I wish to know his name and have him prosecuted according to law."
translations.idiomatic: This censor is surely trying to curry favor by telling you what you want to hear. I ask that he be identified and dealt with according to law."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 國以人為本，聞有災當亟救之，豈可尚復疑之邪！

translations.literal: The state takes people as its foundation; hearing of disaster one should urgently rescue them—how can one still doubt it!
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on its people. When we hear of disaster we should act at once. How can we still be doubting?

sentences.zh: 朕適者不思，失言耳。」

translations.literal: I just now did not think—it was a slip of speech."
translations.idiomatic: I spoke without thinking just now—that was my mistake."

sentences.zh: 命速蠲其租賦。

translations.literal: He ordered that their rents and taxes be quickly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered their rents and levies remitted without delay.

sentences.zh: 上嘗與宰相論治道於延英殿，日旰，暑甚，汗透御服，宰相恐上體倦，求退。

translations.literal: The emperor once discussed the way of governance with the chancellors in the Yanying Hall. The sun was setting, the heat was intense, and sweat soaked through his imperial robes. The chancellors, fearing the emperor was weary in body, asked to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in the Yanying Hall, the emperor debated the principles of governance with his chancellors until sundown. The heat was fierce and sweat soaked his robes. Fearing he was exhausted, the chancellors asked leave to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 上留之曰：「朕入禁中，所與處者獨宮人、宦官耳，故樂與卿等且共談為理之要，殊不知倦也。」

translations.literal: The emperor kept them, saying: "When I enter the inner palace, those I associate with are only palace women and eunuchs. Therefore I delight in talking with you about the essentials of governance—I am not aware of weariness at all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept them. "Inside the palace I have only palace women and eunuchs for company," he said. "That is why I am glad to talk policy with you. I do not feel tired in the least."

sentences.zh: 六月，癸已，司徒、同平章事杜佑以太保致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guisi, Grand Preceptor and Associate Grand Councillor Du You retired as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guisi, Grand Preceptor and Associate Grand Councillor Du You retired to the post of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙亥，立遂王宥為太子，更名恆。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day yihai, Prince Sui You was established as heir apparent and renamed Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on yihai, Prince Sui You was named crown prince and given the name Heng.

sentences.zh: 恆，郭貴妃之子也。

translations.literal: Heng was the son of Consort Guo the Noble Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was the son of Noble Consort Guo.

sentences.zh: 諸姬子澧王寬，長於恆。

translations.literal: Among the consorts' sons, Prince Li Kuan was older than Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Among the sons of the lesser consorts, Prince Li Kuan was older than Heng.

sentences.zh: 上將立恆，命崔群為寬草讓表。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to establish Heng, he ordered Cui Qun to draft for Kuan a memorial of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to name Heng heir, he ordered Cui Qun to draft for Kuan a memorial declining the succession in favor of his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 群曰：「凡推己之有以與人謂之讓。

translations.literal: Qun said: "Generally, pushing what one has to give to others is called yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "To yield is to give up what is rightfully one's own for someone else.

sentences.zh: 遂王，嫡子也，寬何讓焉！」

translations.literal: Prince Sui is the legitimate son—what has Kuan to yield!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sui is the legitimate heir. What could Kuan possibly yield?"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊戌，魏博節度使田季安薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuxu, Weibo military commissioner Tian Ji'an died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuxu, Weibo military commissioner Tian Ji'an died.

sentences.zh: 初，季安娶洺州刺史元誼女，生子懷諫，為節度副使。

translations.literal: Initially, Ji'an married the daughter of Mingzhou prefect Yuan Yi and had a son Huaijian, who served as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ji'an had married the daughter of Mingzhou prefect Yuan Yi. Their son Huaijian served as deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 牙內兵馬使田興，庭玠之子也，有勇力，頗讀書，性恭遜。

translations.literal: Yamen inner corps commander Tian Xing was the son of Tingjie—possessing courage and strength, he read books considerably, and his nature was respectful and modest.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xing, commander of the inner guard corps, was Tingjie's son. He was brave and strong, well read, and by nature courteous and unassuming.

sentences.zh: 季安淫虐，興數規諫，軍中賴之。

translations.literal: Ji'an was debauched and cruel; Xing repeatedly remonstrated, and the army relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an was licentious and brutal. Xing remonstrated with him again and again, and the army came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 季安以為收眾心，出為臨清鎮將，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Ji'an, thinking to win the hearts of the masses, sent him out as garrison commandant of Linqing, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an, thinking to win the troops' loyalty back, posted him as commandant of the Linqing garrison while planning to kill him.

sentences.zh: 興陽為風痺，灸灼滿身，乃得免。

translations.literal: Xing feigned wind paralysis; with moxibustion burns covering his whole body, he then managed to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Xing feigned crippling rheumatism and covered himself with moxibustion burns from head to foot. Only then did he escape death.

sentences.zh: 季安病風，殺戮無度，軍政廢亂。

translations.literal: Ji'an was ill with wind disease; his slaughter knew no bounds, and military administration fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an was stricken with paralysis. He killed without restraint, and military administration collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 夫人元氏召諸將立懷諫為副大使，知軍務，時年十一。

translations.literal: The lady Yuan summoned the generals and established Huaijian as deputy commissioner, to manage military affairs — he was then eleven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuan summoned the generals and had Huaijian installed as deputy commissioner to manage military affairs. He was eleven years old.

sentences.zh: 遷季安於別寢，月餘而薨。

translations.literal: Ji'an was moved to a separate lodging; a little more than a month later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an was moved to a separate wing of the residence. A little over a month later he died.

sentences.zh: 召田興為步射都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Tian Xing was summoned to be chief controller of military affairs for the foot archers.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xing was recalled and made chief controller of military affairs for the foot archers.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以左龍武大將軍薛平為鄭滑節度使，欲為控制魏博。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Left Dragon Martial Grand General Xue Ping was made military commissioner of Zheng-Hua, intending thereby to control Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Left Dragon Martial Grand General Xue Ping was appointed military commissioner of the Zheng-Hua Circuit, with the aim of keeping Weibo in check.

sentences.zh: 上與宰相議魏博事，李吉甫請興兵討之，李絳以為魏博不必用兵，當自歸朝廷。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed Weibo affairs with the chief councillors. Li Jifu requested raising troops to punish it; Li Jiang held that Weibo need not be subjected to arms and would return to the court of itself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief councillors on Weibo. Li Jifu urged raising troops to punish the circuit, but Li Jiang argued that force was unnecessary and that Weibo would come back to the court on its own.

sentences.zh: 吉甫盛陳不可不用兵之狀，上曰：「朕意亦以為然。」

translations.literal: Jifu strongly set forth the case that arms could not be dispensed with. The emperor said: "My mind too holds it so."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu forcefully made the case that military action was unavoidable. The emperor said, "I am inclined to agree."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「臣竊觀兩河蕃鎮之跋扈者，皆分兵以隸諸將，不使專在一人，恐其權任太重，乘間而謀己故也。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Your subject has privately observed that among the overbearing frontier commands of the Two He, all divide troops and assign them to various generals, not letting power rest solely in one man — fearing that authority and duty grow too heavy and that he will seize an opening to plot against them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said, "I have observed that the arrogant circuits of the Two He all divide their troops among their generals rather than concentrating command in one man. They fear that too much power in one pair of hands will give that man the opening to turn against them.

sentences.zh: 諸將勢均力敵，莫能相制，欲廣相連結，則眾心不同，其謀必洩；

translations.literal: The generals are evenly matched in strength and none can control another; if they wish broadly to join in league, then the hearts of the masses differ and the plot is sure to leak out;
translations.idiomatic: Their generals are evenly matched and cannot check one another. If they try to join in a wide conspiracy, their hearts will not align and the plot is bound to leak out;

sentences.zh: 欲獨起為變，則兵少力微，勢必不成。

translations.literal: if one wishes to rise alone in revolt, then troops are few and strength slight — the thing is sure not to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: if one tries to rebel alone, his forces are too few and too weak—the attempt is doomed to fail.

sentences.zh: 加以購賞既重，刑誅又峻，是以諸將互相顧忌，莫敢先發，跋扈者恃此以為長策。

translations.literal: Added to this, rewards for turning are heavy and punishments severe; therefore the generals mutually watch and fear one another and none dares act first — the overbearing rely on this as their long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that, the rewards for betrayal are heavy and the punishments severe. The generals eye one another with suspicion and none dares move first. The arrogant count on this as their long game.

sentences.zh: 然臣竊思之，若常得嚴明主帥能制諸將之死命者以臨之，則粗能自固矣。

translations.literal: Yet your subject has privately reflected: if one could always obtain a strict and clear commander-in-chief able to hold the generals' lives and deaths in his hand to oversee them, then they could roughly keep themselves secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have considered this: so long as a stern, capable commander who holds his generals' lives in his hand remains in charge, the arrangement can more or less hold.

sentences.zh: 今懷諫乳臭子，不能自聽斷，軍府大權必有所歸，諸將厚薄不均，怨怒必起，不相服從，則向日分兵之策，適足為今日禍亂之階也。

translations.literal: Now Huaijian is a milk-smelling child unable to decide for himself; the great power of the military prefecture is sure to go somewhere. The generals are treated unevenly; resentment and anger are sure to rise and they will not obey one another — then the policy of dividing troops of former days is exactly enough to serve as the stairway to today's calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Now Huaijian is only a child in swaddling clothes who cannot rule for himself. The prefecture's real power must fall to someone else. With the generals treated unequally, resentment is inevitable, obedience will break down, and the old policy of dividing the army will become the very ladder to disaster.

sentences.zh: 田氏不為屠肆，則悉為俘囚矣，何煩天兵哉！

translations.literal: If the Tian clan do not become a slaughterhouse, then all will become captives and prisoners — why trouble the heavenly troops!
translations.idiomatic: The Tian clan will either butcher one another or end up as each other's prisoners. Why should the court send imperial troops at all?

sentences.zh: 彼自列將起代主帥，鄰道所惡，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: They, rising from the ranks of generals to replace the commander-in-chief — nothing is more hated by neighboring circuits than this.
translations.idiomatic: For a mere general to rise up and replace his commander is the thing neighboring circuits hate most of all.

sentences.zh: 彼不倚朝廷之援以自存，則立為鄰道所齏粉矣。

translations.literal: If they do not rely on the court's aid to preserve themselves, then at once they will be ground to powder by neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot lean on the court's support to survive, neighboring circuits will crush them at once.

sentences.zh: 故臣以為不必用兵，可坐待魏博之自歸也。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject holds that arms need not be used; one may sit and wait for Weibo to return of itself.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I believe force is unnecessary. We can simply wait for Weibo to return to the court on its own.

sentences.zh: 但願陛下按兵養威，嚴敕諸道選練士馬以須後敕。

translations.literal: Your subject only wishes that Your Majesty hold the army in check and nurture authority, sternly order the various circuits to select and drill soldiers and horses to await later command.
translations.idiomatic: All I ask is that Your Majesty hold your armies back and build up your prestige, and sternly order every circuit to select and drill troops and horses against the day you may need them.

sentences.zh: 使賊中知之，不過數月，必有自效於軍中者矣。

translations.literal: Let the rebels within know this — within no more than a few months there will surely be one who offers himself to the army's service.
translations.idiomatic: Let word of this reach the rebels. Within a few months someone in their ranks is sure to offer himself to us.

sentences.zh: 至時，惟在朝廷應之敏速，中其機會，不愛爵祿以賞其人，使兩河籓鎮聞之，恐其麾下效之以取朝廷之賞，必皆恐懼，爭為恭順矣。

translations.literal: When the time comes, it rests only with the court to respond swiftly, hit the opportunity, not begrudge ranks and emoluments to reward the man, and let the feudal commands of the Two He hear of it — fearing that their subordinates will imitate him to obtain the court's rewards, all will surely be afraid and vie to become respectful and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: When that moment comes, the court need only act swiftly, seize the opening, and reward the man generously with rank and emoluments. Once the circuits of the Two He hear of it, they will fear that their own subordinates will follow his example for the court's reward. Every one of them will be terrified—and scramble to show obedience.

sentences.zh: 此所謂不戰而屈人兵者也。」

translations.literal: This is what is called subduing others' armies without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant by defeating the enemy without fighting."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 他日，吉甫復於延英盛陳用兵之利，且言芻糧金帛皆已有備。

translations.literal: Another day, Jifu again in the Yanying Hall strongly set forth the advantages of using arms, and moreover said that fodder, grain, gold, and silk were all already prepared.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, Jifu again expounded at length in the Yanying Hall on the advantages of war, adding that fodder, grain, money, and silk were all ready.

sentences.zh: 上顧問絳，絳對曰：「兵不可輕動。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to question Jiang; Jiang replied: "Arms must not be lightly moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Li Jiang for his view. Jiang replied, "Troops must not be committed lightly.

sentences.zh: 前年討恆州，四面發兵二十萬，又發兩神策兵自京師赴之，天下騷動，所費七百餘萬緡，訖無成功，為天下笑。

translations.literal: The year before last in punishing Hengzhou, troops were dispatched on four sides to the number of two hundred thousand; moreover two Divine Strategy armies were sent from the capital to join them. The empire was thrown into turmoil; the cost exceeded seven million strings of cash — in the end there was no success, and it became the laughingstock of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Two years ago we marched on Hengzhou. Two hundred thousand men were mobilized on every side, and two Divine Strategy armies were sent from the capital as well. The empire was thrown into turmoil. The campaign cost more than seven million strings of cash and ended in complete failure—the laughingstock of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今瘡痍未復，人皆憚戰，若又以敕命驅之，臣恐非直無功，或生他變。

translations.literal: Now the wounds are not yet healed and all men fear battle; if they are again driven by imperial command, your subject fears not only that there will be no success but that other changes may arise.
translations.idiomatic: The wounds of that campaign have not healed. Everyone dreads war. If we drive them again by imperial command, I fear we will not merely fail—we may trigger something worse.

sentences.zh: 況魏博不必用兵，事勢明白，願陛下勿疑。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Weibo need not be subjected to arms — the situation is clear. Your subject wishes that Your Majesty not doubt it."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the case for leaving Weibo alone is plain. I beg Your Majesty not to doubt it."

sentences.zh: 上奮身撫案曰：「朕不用兵決矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor straightened up and struck the table, saying: "I have decided not to use arms."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat bolt upright and smote the table. "I have made up my mind not to go to war."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「陛下雖有是言，恐退朝之後，復有熒惑聖聽者。」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Though Your Majesty speaks thus, your subject fears that after leaving court there will again be those who dazzle and confuse the holy hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said, "Your Majesty has spoken plainly, but I fear that after court someone may again mislead you."

sentences.zh: 上正色厲聲曰：「朕志已決，誰能惑也！」

translations.literal: The emperor, with stern countenance and stern voice, said: "My resolve is already settled — who can confuse me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face hardened and his voice sharpened. "My mind is made up. Who could sway me now?"

sentences.zh: 絳乃拜賀曰：「此社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: Jiang then bowed in congratulation and said: "This is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang bowed in congratulation. "This is the fortune of the realm."

sentences.zh: 既而田懷諫幼弱，軍政皆決於家僮蔣士則，數以愛憎移易諸將，眾皆憤怒。

translations.literal: Before long, Tian Huaijian was young and weak; military and administrative affairs were all decided by the household slave Jiang Shize, who repeatedly shifted generals according to likes and dislikes, and all were angry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it became clear that Tian Huaijian was too young to rule. Military and civil affairs fell entirely to the household slave Jiang Shize, who repeatedly reshuffled the generals according to his personal likes and dislikes. The whole army seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 朝命久未至，軍中不安。

translations.literal: Court orders long did not arrive; unease spread in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Court orders were long in coming, and unrest spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 田興晨入府，士卒數千人大噪，環興而拜，請為留後。

translations.literal: Tian Xing entered the headquarters in the morning; several thousand troops made a great clamor, encircled Xing and bowed, and requested that he be acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: One morning Tian Xing entered headquarters. Several thousand soldiers raised a great uproar, surrounded him, and bowed, asking him to become acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 興驚僕於地，眾不散。

translations.literal: Xing was startled and fell to the ground; the crowd did not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was so startled he fell to the ground, but the crowd would not disperse.

sentences.zh: 久之，興度不免，乃謂眾曰：「汝肯聽吾言乎！」

translations.literal: After a long while, Xing reckoned there was no escape and therefore said to the crowd: "Will you be willing to heed my words!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Xing saw there was no escape. He said to the crowd, "Will you listen to what I have to say?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「惟命。」

translations.literal: All said: "Only command us."
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Your word is our command."

sentences.zh: 興曰：「勿犯副大使，守朝廷法令，申版籍，請官吏，然後可。」

translations.literal: Xing said: "Do not offend against the deputy commissioner; observe the court's laws and orders; submit registers of households; request court officials — then it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "Do not harm the deputy commissioner. Observe the court's laws, submit the household registers, and request court-appointed officials. Then I will accept."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: All said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 興乃殺蔣士則等十餘人，遷懷諫於外。

translations.literal: Xing then killed Jiang Shize and more than ten others and moved Huaijian outside.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then executed Jiang Shize and more than ten others and had Huaijian moved out of headquarters.

translations.idiomatic: Category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
